item.title: Iran court sentences filmmaker Panahi to five years: media
item.description:
IRAN-CRISIS/COURT-PANAHI

An Iranian court has sentenced renowned filmmaker Jafar Panahi in absentia to over five years in prison, Iranian media said quoting his lawyer, although the latest charges remain unclear.

"The Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced my client to five years and one month in prison and ordered the confiscation of all his movable and immovable property," the ISNA news agency reported, citing his lawyer Mostafa Nili on Tuesday.

"The court also imposed a two-year ban on social media activity and a two-year travel ban," he added.

The ISNA report did not specify the charges.

Iran sentences director Jafar Panahi to year in prison: lawyer

Nili said he discovered the conviction after Panahi told him last week that his bank accounts had been frozen, prompting the lawyer to visit the sentence enforcement office of the Culture and Media Prosecutor's Office.

The lawyer said Panahi had returned to Iran during the war with Israel and the United States which broke out on 28 February.

It remains unclear if Panahi has remained in Iran.

Panahi currently has three pending cases, Nili said, adding that his client had not been notified of the hearing date in the latest case.

In June, an Iranian court rejected Panahi's appeal against a one-year sentence in one of the cases, which was handed down in December on charges of "propaganda" against Iran.

Panahi, 66, won the top prize at last year's Cannes film festival for "It Was Just an Accident", a film in which five ex-inmates contemplate whether to exact revenge on a man they believe to be their former jailer.

He has won a host of prizes at European film festivals since showcasing his debut film "The White Balloon" in Cannes in 1995, which won an award for best first feature.

In 2010, Panahi was banned from making movies for 20 years, and from leaving the country, after supporting mass anti-government protests a year earlier and making a series of films that critiqued the state of modern Iran.

Iranian director Jafar Panahi released after hunger strike

Convicted of "propaganda against the system", he was sentenced to six years in jail but served only two months behind bars before being released on bail.

A year later, he dispatched a documentary with the title "This is Not a Film" to the Cannes festival on a flash drive stashed in a cake.

His 2015 movie "Taxi" featured him acting as a taxi driver and was shot entirely in a car.

In 2022, he was arrested in connection with protests by a group of filmmakers but was released nearly seven months later.

Iranian filmmakers, prominent media figures and celebrities are closely monitored in Iran and their work reviewed for content deemed critical of the Islamic republic.

item.title: PM's flight departs Narita for Dhaka after five-hour delay due to technical fault
item.description:
The Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his entourage has departed from Japan’s Narita International Airport for Dhaka, five hours behind schedule, after a technical fault delayed its departure.

The flight took off for Dhaka at around 10:45 pm local time in Japan on Thursday. A member of the prime minister’s entourage confirmed the information to Prothom Alo.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his entourage were scheduled to leave Japan for Dhaka at around 6:00 pm local time on Thursday after a four-day visit. However, the aircraft could not depart as scheduled due to a technical fault.

Mechanical fault delays PM’s flight from Japan to Dhaka

After the fault was repaired, the aircraft was ready for departure at around 10:15 pm local time. The flight subsequently left for Dhaka at around 10:45 pm.

Earlier, in a press release issued around 5:00 pm, Biman Bangladesh Airlines said flight BG 377, carrying the prime minister and his entourage, had been delayed in taking off from Narita International Airport for Dhaka due to a technical fault. The airline’s flight operations and engineering teams were working to resolve the problem.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived in Tokyo, the Japanese capital, on 26 October on a four-day state visit at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The prime minister is returning home on Thursday after completing the visit.

PM seeks Japan’s help in Bangladesh exports diversification

In a press release sent at 8:34 pm, Biman’s public relations department later said flight BG 377, carrying the prime minister and his entourage, had safely taken off from Narita International Airport for Dhaka after the technical fault was repaired.

According to the release, the aircraft took off at 7:55 pm Bangladesh time. It is scheduled to land in Dhaka at 3:00 am on 30 October.

Biman’s engineers and Japanese technicians repaired the fault. Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat and Biman’s deputy managing director were present during the process.

item.title: GP inaugurates Bangladesh’s largest data centre solar plant
item.description:
Grameenphone, the country’s leading telecommunications service provider, has inaugurated a 325 kilowatt-peak (KWp) solar power plant at its Sylhet Data Centre, marking a significant step towards expanding the use of renewable energy across its operations, reports a press release.

Developed by Grameenphone, with ZTE as the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) provider, the installation comprises 450 high-efficiency solar panels and is the largest solar power plant at any data centre in Bangladesh.

The newly inaugurated solar plant is expected to generate more than 300 megawatt-hours (MWh) of electricity annually, reducing approximately 188 tonnes of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions each year.

By integrating renewable energy into its data centre operations, Grameenphone aims to reduce its environmental footprint while supporting the growing demand for digital connectivity and services through more sustainable infrastructure – in line with the company’s vision to reduce CO₂ emissions by 50 per cent by 2030, compared to its 2019 baseline.

The solar plant was inaugurated by Yasir Azman, chief executive officer of Grameenphone, in the presence of Grameenphone’s Chief Technology Officer Abul Kasem Mohiuddin Al-Amin, Chief Financial Officer Otto Magne Risbakk and Chief Marketing Officer Farha Naz Zaman, along with Mao Junyong, chief executive officer of ZTE Bangladesh, at the Sylhet Data Centre.

Speaking on the occasion, Yasir Azman, chief executive officer of Grameenphone, said, “As Bangladesh continues its digital transformation, we recognise the importance of building infrastructure that is not only reliable and future-ready but also environmentally responsible. At Grameenphone, we have set a clear ambition to reduce our CO₂ emissions by 50 per cent by 2030, compared to our 2019 baseline. Achieving this requires us to continuously explore cleaner energy solutions and integrate sustainable practices across our operations. The solar plant at our Sylhet Data Centre is a tangible step in this journey, demonstrating how we can reduce our environmental impact while strengthening the digital infrastructure that serves millions of customers. We will continue to invest in sustainable and innovative solutions that create long-term value for our customers, society and the environment.”

Mao Junyong, chief executive officer of ZTE Bangladesh said, “We are proud to partner with Grameenphone in launching Bangladesh’s largest solar power plant at a data center. This project demonstrates how advanced technology and renewable energy can come together to create more energy-efficient and sustainable digital infrastructure. By integrating high-efficiency solar solutions into data center operations, we are helping reduce CO₂ emissions in line with Grameenphone’s sustainability goals. We believe this collaboration will set an example for the industry and contribute to building a greener and more sustainable digital future for Bangladesh.”

The initiative reflects Grameenphone’s continued focus on embedding sustainability into its business operations and investing in solutions that can deliver both operational and environmental benefits.

Through greater adoption of renewable energy, energy-efficient technologies and responsible resource management, the company aims to support a lower-carbon digital future for Bangladesh.

item.title: Bangladesh spinners restore balance after batting collapse
item.description:
Bangladesh's spinners revived their side's hopes after a disappointing batting collapse, leaving the opening Test against West Indies finely poised at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium today.

After bowling out Bangladesh for 272 in the first innings, West Indies made a promising start in reply but lost four wickets to the spin duo of Taijul Islam and Mehidy Hasan Miraz to reach 134-4 at stumps on the Day 2, which was curtailed by bad light and rain.

Tagenarine Chanderpaul was unbeaten on 43, while Justin Greaves was batting on 15 when play was called off due to bad light.

Opener John Campbell struck a fluent half-century to give the side a solid before Bangladesh spinners helped the claw back into the contest.

Campbell who raised his sixth Test half-century with a towering six off Mehidy Hasan Miraz through long-on region was finally out on 54, allowing Bangladesh regain some momentum.

Pacer Hasan Mahmud gave Bangladesh the initial success by dismissing Brandon King for 15.

Campbell and Chanderpaul, the son of West Indies great Shivnarine Chanderpaul, kept the side in the hunt-with Campbell attacking the bowlers and Chanderpaul showing a patience like monk.

But the disruption firstly caused by bad light and then rain appeared to be a distraction for Campbell.

The game restarted after an hour brought a luck for Bangladesh. Miraz struck immediately after resumption with flighted delivery which Campbell poked to second slip, where skipper Shanto dived forward to take an excellent catch.

Taijul then struck twice in the same over, claiming the wicket of Kevam Hodge (7) and Aamir Jangoo for duck, leaving West Indies at 97-4.

However, Chanderpaul who played 145 balls for his 43 so far and Greaves saw out the day without further trouble, denying Bangladesh full control.

Earlier, resuming the day at 213-3, Bangladesh experienced a sensational
collapse which saw them lost the last seven wickets for 59 runs in the
morning session to be out all out for 272.

Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican was the wrecker-in-chief, claiming 5-53 to
hasten Bangladesh collapse.

Shadman Islam who was stranded on 99, reached his third century off 221
balls, with doubles off Joshua Bishop in the second ball of the innings.

Soon after Bishop, the left-arm spinner, reviewed one successfully to remove Shadman for his debut wicket and followed it up with the wicket of Towhid Hridoy by delivering an excellent straighter. By doing so he ended his debut innings with 2-61.

Hridoy who was forced to leave the ground yesterday with a muscle cramp
returned to resume batting after Shadman''s dismissal but couldn't add any run to his 42.

After his dismissal, Bangladesh suddenly found them in awkward situation by reeling to 221-5 but Liton and Mehidy Hasan Miraz looked solid in the crease, offering the side some hopes.

Warrican turned one sharply to rattle the stump of Miraz, dismissing him for 15.

Shamar Joseph who ended with 2-41, dealt a double blow with the wicket of Nayeem Hasan and Hasan Murad.

Warrican came back to complete his fourth five-wicket haul by dismissing
Taijul Islam and Shoriful Islam as Bangladesh lost last five wickets for 19
runs, leaving Liton stranded on 34 at the other end.

item.title: Tahsif told mother ‘coming home’ after repeated calls; body found in Turag River next day
item.description:
Former Air Force flight lieutenant Tahsif Souri spent the day shopping with his mother. He also bought some things for his father. In the evening, he left home after a call from a younger friend he was close to.

Later that night, he sent his mother a message saying he was coming home. But he never returned. The following afternoon, Wednesday, police recovered his body floating in the Turag River.

His motorcycle has also been missing since Tahsif’s death. A relative said he had left home on it on Tuesday. These details about the events leading up to Tahsif’s disappearance emerged from conversations with his father, KM Eneyetul Karim, and a relative.

Tahsif lived in the Korobi building at the Rajuk Apartment Project in Sector 18 of Uttara, in the capital. His father, Eneyetul Karim, told Prothom Alo that on Tuesday evening, Dwip, a younger friend whom Tahsif was close to, came downstairs to call him. Tahsif went down, saying he would talk to Dwip and return shortly. He never came back home.

Ex-Air Force officer’s body recovered from Turag River

When Tahsif did not return home, his mother called his mobile phone several times but could not reach him. At around 1:35 am, he sent her a message saying he was coming home. However, his father, Eneyetul Karim, said the message gave the impression that his son was busy.

As Tahsif still had not returned, the family continued searching for him. On Wednesday afternoon, his father went to Turag police station, but the police had no information about his son at the time. At around 5:15 pm, he received a call from Uttarkhan police station informing him that Tahsif’s body has been recovered.

Earlier on Wednesday afternoon, the Tongi River Police outpost had recovered Tahsif’s body from the Turag River near Rajabari Ghat. Enayetul Karim said the family had no reason to believe that Tahsif ever used to visit the area where his body was recovered.

Motorcycle still missing

Tahsif was the eldest of two brothers and a sister. He owned a motorcycle and had been involved in a motorcycle accident about a month earlier. After that, his family had told him not to ride the motorcycle anymore.

A relative said Tahsif had taken the motorcycle with him when he left home on Tuesday. The family has not been able to find out where it is.

The relative said, “We have also spoken to Dwip. But Tahsif’s bike is missing. The police asked us for the bike’s details and photographs. We have provided them. The police will be able to say more about this.”

Family members have also spoken to Dwip to find out what happened to Tahsif that day. According to the relatives, Dwip told them that he had eaten with Tahsif on Tuesday night. He then dropped Tahsif near his residential area before leaving.

Ex-Air Force officer Tahsif identified through mobile phone found with body

Worked at BCB and Netra News

Tahsif had served as a flight lieutenant in the Air Force. His family said he later lost his job.

Tahsif’s father, Eneyetul Karim said that a “disciplinary” issue had been cited as the reason for his son’s dismissal from the Air Force. Tahsif subsequently worked at the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) and Netra News.

Describing his son’s nature, Eneyetul Karim said, “He was extremely gentle by nature and sociable. He had good relationships with everyone, both seniors and juniors.”

Meanwhile, no case has yet been filed over the recovery of Tahsif’s body. Habibur Rahman, officer-in-charge (OC) of Uttarkhan police station, told Prothom Alo that they have not received any complaint. The River Police are investigating the matter.

Firoz Uddin, an inspector at the Tongi River Police outpost, told Prothom Alo that no case has yet been filed in connection with the incident. All aspects related to the incident were being investigated.

item.title: Ministry forms committee to investigate incident involving Manik Pashari in Pirojpur
item.description:
The Ministry of Liberation War Affairs has formed a three-member committee to investigate what happened surrounding the burial of freedom fighter Manik Pashari following his death in Chitolia village in Pirojpur. The committee will look into who was involved in the incident. It will also verify Pashari’s freedom fighter certificate.

The ministry disclosed the information in a press release on Thursday.

According to the release, the ministry has taken note of reports published in various media outlets. In view of the issues raised in those reports, an investigation committee has been formed under the instructions of Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan to establish the facts and verify the relevant matters.

An additional secretary of the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs will head the committee. The other two members will be a deputy secretary of the ministry and a member of the National Freedom Fighters Council (Jamuka).

The committee will investigate the circumstances surrounding Pashari’s death, verify the authenticity of his freedom fighter certificate and examine other related matters. It will determine whether his certificate was issued properly. The committee will also investigate who was behind the incident and establish what actually happened. If necessary, it will collect information from the deputy commissioner (DC) and upazila nirbahi officers (UNOs) concerned.

The ministry said in the press release that the committee had been instructed to complete the investigation promptly and submit its report to the ministry. Further action will be taken in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations after reviewing the committee’s findings and recommendations.

Ministry stresses protection of freedom fighters’ dignity

In the press release, the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs said it operates in accordance with the spirit and ideals of the Liberation War. To uphold the spirit and dignity of the Liberation War, the ministry is working to remove the names of non-freedom fighters from the official list. At the same time, it has made its position clear that the honour and dignity of genuine freedom fighters must not be undermined.

The release further stated that if any freedom fighter engages in unethical activities or is used by an organisation or group, they must bear responsibility for their actions. The ministry is also vigilant to ensure that no fraudulent individual or group can use the names of those who fought in the Liberation War to push the state into a crisis.

Manik Pashari had testified against Delawar Hossain Sayedee, a former leader of Jamaat-e-Islami, before the International Crimes Tribunal in a crimes against humanity case relating to 1971.

Family members said Pashari had been staying at his son-in-law’s house in Tungipara, Gopalganj, since 5 August 2024. After suffering from illness for two months, he died there at around 10am on 24 October.

Tensions over burial

Tensions erupted on Saturday over the decision to accord Manik Pashari a guard of honour in Pirojpur. Some local residents demanded that he not be buried there. During this time, Jamaat-e-Islami leaders and activists were seen gathering and taking positions at various key locations in Pirojpur town.

However, Pirojpur district Jamaat-e-Islami secretary Zahirul Haque said at the time, “We did not oppose Manik Pashari’s burial. However, we did not provide any assistance with it either. We know nothing about whose patronage the burial took place under or how it was carried out with the administration’s assistance.”

item.title: Inside Baihetan: China’s mega dam powering 75 million homes
item.description:
Wedged into a steep gorge on the Jinsha River, China’s Baihetan Hydropower Station had generated more than 250 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity by June 2026, according to its operators.

They call it the world’s largest clean energy corridor, one that has met the household demand of 75 million people.

“This is the largest clean energy corridor of the world, which met the household demand of 75 million people,” Luo Yuanwang, Shift Supervisor of Shift 1, Operations Department of Baihetan Hyropower Station, told Prothom Alo on Wednesday.

While talking to him during the visit of the Baihetan Hydropower Station, he told this reporter that currently some 400 people working in the project.

Project overview

Baihetan Hydropower Station is the second of the four hydropower cascade projects downstream of the Jinsha River, following Wudongde and preceding Xiluodu and Xiangjiaba.

It is located in Ningnan County, Sichuan Province, and Qiaojia County, Yunnan Province, approximately 182 km from Wudongde and 195 km upstream of Xiluodu Hydropower Station.

The project controls a catchment area of 430,300 square kilometres, accounting for 91 per cent of the Jinsha River basin upstream of the dam site.

The primary purpose of Baihetan Hydropower Station is electricity generation, while also serving flood control and navigation functions and promoting local economic and social development.

The reservoir has a total storage capacity of 20.627 billion cubic metres including 10.436 billion cubic metres of regulating storage and 7.5 billion cubic metres of flood-control storage.

Electricity generation is the main purpose, but the station also provides flood control and navigation benefits and supports economic and social development in the surrounding region

The power station has an installed capacity of 16,000 MW, with an average annual power generation of 62.443 billion kWh and a guaranteed output of 5,500 MW.

The project’s major structures comprise the river-blocking dam, flood-discharge and energy-dissipation facilities, and the water-conveyance and power-generation system.

The dam is a concrete double-curvature arch dam, with a crest elevation of 834.00 metres and a maximum height of 289.00 metres. Its foundation includes a cushion slab and two auxiliary dams.

The flood-discharge and energy-dissipation facilities consist of six surface outlets in the dam body, seven deep outlets, and three flood-discharge tunnels on the left bank.

The underground powerhouse is symmetrically arranged on the left and right banks, with each powerhouse containing eight 1,000 MW Francis turbine-generator units. During construction, diversion through tunnels was maintained throughout the year.

Clean energy push

Officials and operators at the site present Baihetan as a symbol of China’s push towards large-scale clean energy. Hydropower of this scale, they say, supplies stable, low-carbon electricity to distant load centres while also helping manage floods on one of the country’s major rivers.

Harsh Natural Conditions, Complex Geology and Formidable Construction Challenges

Complex climatic conditions: The project site experiences extreme weather, with maximum air temperatures reaching 43°C, ground-surface temperatures approaching 70°C, and maximum wind forces reaching Beaufort Force 13.

Steep terrain at the dam site: The site lies within an asymmetrical V-shaped valley, making project planning and layout exceptionally difficult.

Unprecedented foundation geology: For the first time, a dam foundation was constructed on columnar-jointed basalt characterized by hard, brittle and highly fractured rock, making excavation relatively easy.

World-leading underground powerhouse scale: The underground powerhouse cavern complex ranks first in the world in terms of span. Surrounding rock stability posed particularly significant challenges.

High geological disaster risks: The project hub area faces substantial risks from geological hazards, including landslides and debris flows. The project is also subject to stringent seismic design and fortification requirements.

Project stats

In 1991, Preliminary work on Baihetan Hydropower Station commenced in full.

In October 2010, the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) approved preliminary work on Baihetan Hydropower Station.

In December 2010, the Sichuan Provincial People's Government issued the project’s construction approval document, followed by the Yunnan Provincial People's Government in January 2011.

In June 2011, China Three Gorges Corporation began preparatory work for the project. River closure was achieved in November 2015.

August 2017, Full-scale construction of the main works commenced.

In May 2021, Concrete placement for the main dam was completed to the crest, and reservoir impoundment began.

In June 2021, the first batch of generating units was commissioned.

In December 2022, all generating units were commissioned.

In June 2023, the project was completed in June 2023.

item.title: Nuclear fuel supply begins for Rooppur plant’s second unit
item.description:
Preparations have begun for the initial fuel loading of the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, with the first shipment of fuel assemblies for its VVER-1200 reactor arriving in Bangladesh, Russia’s state nuclear corporation Rosatom has said.
According to a Rosatom press release, the fuel was manufactured at the Novosibirsk Chemical Concentrates Plant in Siberia and transported to Bangladesh by a specialised cargo aircraft. Upon arrival at the Rooppur project site, the fuel containers were placed in designated storage facilities.
Before loading into the reactor, each fuel assembly will undergo a technical inspection by a joint commission comprising representatives from Bangladesh, the project’s general contractor and the fuel manufacturer. The process will follow nuclear and radiation safety protocols, the release said.
A separate shipment of fresh fuel for the first unit’s upcoming refuelling has also arrived in Bangladesh. Refuelling is scheduled to take place after the first unit completes its initial fuel cycle.
Rosatom said initial fuel loading for the first unit’s reactor core was completed in 2026. The reactor reached its minimum controllable power level this month.
Before the unit can supply electricity to the national grid, it must undergo a series of power-escalation tests and receive approval from the regulatory authority.
The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has two Generation III+ VVER-1200 reactors based on Russian designs, with a combined generation capacity of 2,400MW. Rosatom’s engineering division serves as the project’s principal designer and contractor.

item.title: Hanif sentenced to death for crimes against humanity in Kushtia
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced Mahbubul Alam Hanif, a joint general secretary of the now-banned Awami League, to death for crimes against humanity, including the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July mass uprising.
Three other defendants in the case have been sentenced to imprisonment for the remainder of their lives.
The verdict was delivered on Thursday by a three-member panel of International Crimes Tribunal-2, led by Chairman Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury.
The tribunal found Hanif guilty on counts 1 to 6 of the first charge and sentenced him to death. He was also found guilty of the second and third charges and sentenced to life imprisonment with hard labour.
The three other defendants — Md Sadar Uddin Khan, Md Azgar Ali and Md Ataur Rahman Ata — were found guilty on counts 1 to 6 of the first charge and sentenced to imprisonment for the remainder of their lives with hard labour. They were also sentenced to life imprisonment with hard labour on the second and third charges.
The tribunal found all four defendants guilty of the fourth and fifth charges and sentenced each to life imprisonment with hard labour.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam and other members of the prosecution team were present when the verdict was announced. State-appointed lawyer Amir Hossain represented the defendants, who are currently at large.
The tribunal had reserved the verdict after the prosecution and defence concluded their arguments. October 27 was subsequently set as the date for delivering the judgment.
Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim presented the prosecution's arguments, assisted by Faruk Ahammad, Sahidul Islam Sardar, Abdus Sattar Palwan and others.
Tamim said proceedings against the four accused had concluded, but the prosecution later submitted additional evidence, prompting further arguments. The prosecution sought the maximum punishment for all four defendants.
He alleged that Hanif, as a joint general secretary of the Awami League, was involved in government decision-making to suppress the July mass uprising and coordinated the implementation of those measures through his subordinates.
According to Tamim, Hanif issued directives to his subordinates and coordinated actions through telephone conversations. He also alleged that Hanif took part in key party decisions, supported meetings held by Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and instructed the Kushtia superintendent of police, district and upazila chairmen, and party activists to carry out the killings. The prosecution submitted records of the telephone conversations as evidence, he said.
Tamim also referred to sentences previously handed down by the tribunal to Awami League President Sheikh Hasina, General Secretary Obaidul Quader and Joint General Secretary Bahauddin Nasim for the same offences, arguing that Hanif should receive a similar sentence because of his comparable position.
The other accused are Kushtia District Awami League President Sadar Uddin Khan, district general secretary Azgar Ali and Kushtia city unit general secretary Ataur Rahman Ata. All four defendants are in hiding.
The tribunal formally framed charges against the four accused on November 2, 2025, paving the way for the trial. The prosecution submitted the formal charges on October 5, and the tribunal took cognizance of them the following day.
The charges included making inflammatory statements, conspiracy and the killing of six people in Kushtia. Testimony from 19 witnesses had been completed by April 23, after the investigating officer was cross-examined. The tribunal later reopened arguments after the prosecution submitted additional evidence.

item.title: PM Tarique visits Toyota’s Motomachi plant in Japan

item.title: Body of former flight lieutenant Tahsif Souri recovered in Tongi
item.description:
River police have recovered the body of KM Tahsif Sauri, 28, a former Air Force flight lieutenant, from the Turag River in Dhaka, a day after he went missing.
Uttarkhan police station Officer-in-Charge Habibur Rahman confirmed the recovery to Dhaka Tribune on Thursday morning. He said no case had been filed over the incident as of Thursday morning.
Inspector Firoz Uddin of the River Police’s Tongi outpost said they recovered the body near Rajabari Ghat on the Turag River around 4:30pm on Wednesday after receiving a call through the national emergency helpline 999.
An inquest report was prepared before the body was sent to the morgue at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.
Firoz said Tahsif lived with his family in a flat in Sector 18 of Uttara and went missing on Tuesday. His father’s name is KM Enayet Helal.
He said efforts were underway to determine the circumstances surrounding Tahsif’s death.

item.title: Woman dies amid dowry demands, husband arrested
item.description:
Zumratun Nesa Barsha, 24, video-called her father late at night after allegedly being tortured by her husband over dowry demands. She told her parents about the abuse and pleaded for help. When the call suddenly disconnected, her family went to check on her and learned that she had died.
Barsha’s father, Sheikh Monowar Hossain, filed a murder case with Tejgaon police station following the incident. Police said her husband, Nabid Hossain, had been arrested in connection with the case and sent to court.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Thursday afternoon, Tejgaon police station Officer-in-Charge Muniruzzaman said Nabid allegedly beat Barsha repeatedly over dowry demands. Marks of injuries were found on her body, he added.
Muniruzzaman said Barsha’s father filed the case and Nabid was arrested from a hospital before being sent to court. The investigation is ongoing.
The incident took place at a house in Manipuripara in the capital around midnight on Tuesday. Barsha was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead.
Sheikh Monowar Hossain said Barsha and Nabid had married a year earlier after a relationship. He alleged that Nabid was unemployed and repeatedly demanded money from his father-in-law after the marriage. Barsha’s family had given him money several times, he said, but the demands frequently led to quarrels and physical abuse.
He said Barsha was beaten again over money on Tuesday. According to him, someone from her in-laws’ household recorded the incident and sent the footage to her family.
Unable to bear the abuse, Barsha video-called her father around midnight. She was crying and pleading with her family to take her back to their home, saying she feared they would kill her if she remained there, her father said. The call then disconnected.
Her parents set out for the house that night. When they arrived in Manipuripara around 12:30am, they saw an ambulance outside the house.
Barsha’s family later asked her in-laws what had happened and were told that she had died by suicide.

item.title: Legal notice seeks ban on primary admission tests
item.description:
A legal notice has been served on the government demanding an end to admission tests at the primary level, a ban on unauthorised pre-primary classes such as Play, Nursery, KG-1 and KG-2, and a halt to the use of textbooks beyond those approved by the National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB).
Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun, a Supreme Court lawyer, issued the notice in the public interest on Thursday. It was sent by registered post to the cabinet secretary, the secretary of the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, the director general of the Directorate of Primary Education and the NCTB chairman.
The notice calls for effective measures to address the issues within five days. It warns that failure to act will prompt the filing of a public interest writ petition with the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution to safeguard children's welfare.
Citing Article 17 of the Constitution and the Compulsory Primary Education Act, 1990, the notice says the state is obligated to ensure universal, accessible and compulsory primary education. However, it alleges that commercial interests have increasingly influenced primary education.
According to the notice, children aged three to five are enrolled in multiple stages, including Play, Nursery, KG-1 and KG-2, exposing them to excessive academic work and additional textbooks. The notice argues that this can undermine their childhood, mental development and creativity.
It calls for the discontinuation of unauthorised courses and the retention of a single, government-approved pre-primary grade.
The notice also raises concerns over primary-level admission procedures involving written examinations, screening tests and oral interviews. Mamun argues that competitive admission tests can cause fear and mental stress among young children and undermine their self-confidence. He has therefore demanded the complete abolition of such tests to ensure an inclusive and enjoyable learning environment.
The notice further objects to the use of supplementary materials, including grammar books, workbooks and reference texts, beyond those prescribed by the NCTB. It alleges that some educational institutions work with commercial publishers to impose excessive books and curriculum requirements on children, risking physical fatigue, mental exhaustion and restricted creative development.
It also argues that children should not be subjected to rote learning from an early age. Instead, they should have opportunities to develop independent thinking, imagination and creativity.
According to the notice, excessive academic pressure runs counter to the principles enshrined in Articles 17, 27, 31 and 32 of the Constitution, which address education, equality, legal protection, and the right to life and personal liberty.
The notice demands that unauthorised pre-primary courses be discontinued and primary-level admission tests prohibited within five days. It also calls for punitive measures, including cancellation of registration, against institutions that require textbooks beyond those prescribed by the NCTB.
In addition, it proposes forming monitoring teams at the upazila and district levels to ensure compliance.
The notice warns that a public interest litigation petition will be filed with the High Court if the authorities fail to take the requested steps within the stipulated period.

item.title: DRU awaits prime minister’s decision on IGP’s remarks
item.description:
The Dhaka Reporters Unity (DRU) believes the government has taken note of the controversial remarks made by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir regarding “crossfire” and journalists.
Government representatives have also addressed the issue. Zahed Ur Rahman, the prime minister’s adviser on information and broadcasting, has indicated that the government’s final position will be determined after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returns to the country. Reassured by the statements from government officials, the DRU is now awaiting the prime minister’s decision.
In a statement issued on Thursday, DRU President Abu Saleh Akon and General Secretary Mainul Hasan Sohel conveyed these views on behalf of the organisation’s executive committee.
The statement said the DRU had previously demanded that the IGP retract his controversial remarks about journalists and offer an unconditional apology. However, the IGP has yet to do so, raising serious concerns among members of the journalistic community.
“As a public servant, he has no justification for making such comments about journalists,” the statement said, adding that the DRU would remain firm in defending journalists’ professional dignity and honour, as well as the principle of independent journalism. The organisation expects the government to take appropriate action regarding the IGP’s remarks.
DRU leaders expressed hope that the government would not endorse the IGP’s sweeping and irresponsible comments. They said the head of a vital institution such as the police force should exercise restraint, responsibility and professionalism in public statements. Making broad, unsubstantiated generalisations about any professional group is unacceptable, they added.
The statement further noted that the public remarks of senior officials are closely linked to the image of the state and the government. Intemperate and irresponsible comments can put the government in an embarrassing position both at home and abroad, damage its reputation and raise questions about its commitment to democratic values, freedom of expression and its relationship with the journalistic community.
Journalists serve the public interest by exposing irregularities, corruption and crime, the DRU leaders said. Making sweeping accusations against the entire profession over published news reports threatens the environment for independent journalism.
They added that specific allegations against individual journalists should be addressed through established legal channels and due process. Holding the entire journalistic community accountable for isolated incidents or allegations is neither reasonable nor fair, they said.
The DRU leaders expressed hope that the government would clarify its position on the IGP’s remarks and ensure that officials in positions of responsibility uphold professional decorum and accountability in their public statements.
They reiterated their demand that the IGP retract his remarks and offer an unconditional apology to the journalistic community.

item.title: UGC plans satellite TV channel to expand access to higher education
item.description:
The University Grants Commission (UGC) is planning to launch a dedicated satellite television channel for higher education to reduce disparities in access to educational opportunities across the country.
The commission is considering launching a pilot programme by utilising the existing technological facilities of Bangladesh Open University (BOU), UGC Chairman Professor Dr Mamun Ahmed said on Wednesday.
He disclosed the plan while speaking as a special guest at a discussion marking the 34th founding anniversary of Bangladesh Open University.
The UGC chairman said disparities exist in educational opportunities and academic activities among the country's universities, with some located in urban areas and others in remote regions.
To strengthen connections among teachers and students across these institutions, the UGC plans to introduce a separate television channel dedicated to higher education, he said, adding that a pilot programme could be launched using BOU's existing facilities.
Mamun Ahmed also said the commission plans to bring around 180 public and private universities under a digital network within the next two years.
The initiative will involve developing high-speed internet connectivity, digital classrooms and other facilities needed for digital campuses, he said. It would expand opportunities for academic communication, joint research and collaboration among universities.
The network would also make it possible to connect Bangladeshi teachers and researchers working at foreign universities with higher education institutions in the country, he added.
The UGC chairman said advances in artificial intelligence (AI), data science and online technologies were challenging conventional education systems, making it essential to focus on both knowledge acquisition and skills development.
He stressed the need to ensure quality, technology-driven and skills-based education.
Noting that people can now access educational resources from home through YouTube and other online platforms, Mamun Ahmed said Bangladesh Open University's teaching methods and infrastructure needed to be updated to meet changing circumstances.
He said the UGC and the open university should work together to achieve this goal.
The chairman observed that conventional education systems could not bring people of all ages, social backgrounds and geographical locations under their coverage, leaving many to drop out or remain excluded from mainstream education.
Bangladesh Open University could reach these people by utilising its extensive network, he said. The university currently has around 300,000 students, and enrolment could increase further if quality and skills-based education were ensured.
Mamun Ahmed said the idea of establishing Bangladesh Open University was introduced by Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman and implemented in 1992 during the tenure of then Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
The university has the technological facilities required for distance learning, a full-fledged media centre and a nationwide network to maintain contact with students, he said.
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon attended the programme as the chief guest, while BOU Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Siddiqur Rahman Khan presided over it.
Former Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Emeritus Professor Dr Anwarullah Chowdhury delivered the keynote address.

item.title: Bangladesh win recurve men’s team gold at Asia Cup Archery
item.description:
Bangladesh clinched their second gold medal at the Asia Cup–World Ranking Tournament, Leg 2, after defeating Kazakhstan 6–2 in the recurve men’s team final in Sulaymaniyah, Iraq, on Thursday.
The trio of Abdur Rahman Alif, Md Sagor Islam and Abdulla Al Mohammad Rafi, coached by Frederick Martin, staged a comeback after losing the opening set to secure the title.
Bangladesh lost the first set 50–53 but bounced back to win the second 55–54, before taking the third 55–52 and the fourth 52–51 to complete a 6–2 victory on set points.
The triumph came a day after Bangladesh won gold in the compound women’s team event, with Bonna Akter, Sreeporna Biswas and Kulsum Akter Mone defeating Kazakhstan 230–220 in the final.
The back-to-back gold medals underline Bangladesh’s strong showing at the international tournament, with the archers securing titles in both the recurve men’s and compound women’s team events.
The Bangladesh Archery Federation congratulated the athletes and coaching staff on the latest achievement.

item.title: Argentine football fan jailed for threats over Di Maria return
item.description:
An Argentine court jailed a football supporter for seven and a half years on Wednesday for threatening Angel Di Maria in 2024 in a bid to stop the World Cup winner returning to Argentina at the end of his career.
A court in Rosario found Sergio Di Vanni, 45, guilty of ordering acts of intimidation against Di Maria's family with the aim of dissuading the former Argentina international from returning from abroad to play for a rival club.
Di Maria was playing for Benfica at the time, in March 2024, but was considering a return to his boyhood club Rosario Central, a move he eventually completed in 2025.
Rosario Central and Newell's Old Boys, Lionel Messi's childhood club, are the two major teams in Rosario and fierce local rivals.
The threats included gunshots fired near a gated community where Di Maria owns a property and the dumping of a pig's head bearing a bullet wound outside an estate agency run by his sister, alongside a message threatening his daughter.
A 25-year-old woman, Belen Gutierrez, identified by prosecutors as one of the perpetrators, was sentenced to three and a half years in prison in June after entering a plea agreement.
A third suspect remains in pre-trial detention. Prosecutors alleged the two carried out the threats in exchange for four million pesos ($2,600).
According to the prosecution, the intimidation campaign was linked to an internal power struggle among Newell's ultras. Di Vanni's sentence also covered separate offences related to his involvement in the supporters' group.
Following the threats, Di Maria initially abandoned plans to return to Argentina for the safety of his family.
He ultimately reversed that decision and, now 38, has spent the past two seasons at Rosario Central, helping the club win the Argentine title at the end of 2025.

item.title: Djokovic wins Basel opener to boost ATP Finals bid
item.description:
Novak Djokovic dug deep to overcome Ugo Humbert in three sets in his opening match in Basel on Wednesday, keeping his bid to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals on course.
The 39-year-old Djokovic dropped the first set but recovered to beat the French left-hander 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 on his first appearance in Basel since 2011.
"It was a super tight match, very intense from the beginning," said Djokovic.
"I was under attack from the very first point. I had to weather the storm, but I managed to find my rhythm at the beginning of the second set.
"After that, I started feeling a bit more comfortable with his tempo. Overall, it was a huge challenge. I succeeded in managing to find the solutions in a tough match today."
Djokovic strengthened his chances of a record 19th qualification for the ATP Finals by winning the China Open in Beijing earlier this month, the 102nd title of his career.
That was followed by an early exit at the Shanghai Masters, with the 24-time Grand Slam champion accepting a wild card into the Swiss event after slipping to 11th in the Race to Turin standings.
Djokovic is a seven-time winner of the ATP Finals, but he did not compete at either of the past two editions because of injury. Only the top eight players qualify for the November 15-22 showpiece, although Jannik Sinner has already pulled out due to a knee problem.
Fourth seed Djokovic takes on Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff in the next round in Basel. He holds an 8-0 record against Struff.

item.title: Warrican five-for bowls Bangladesh out for 272
item.description:
A reckless batting show triggered a sensational collapse as Bangladesh lost seven wickets for 59 runs in the morning session of Day 2 to be all out for 272 in the first cricket Test against West Indies at Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium today.
Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican was the wrecker-in-chief, claiming 5-53 to hasten Bangladesh's collapse after the hosts resumed at 213-3.
Shadman Islam who was stranded on 99, reached his third century off 221 balls, with doubles off Joshua Bishop in the second ball of the innings.
Soon after Bishop, the left-arm spinner, reviewed one successfully to remove Shadman for his debut wicket and followed it up with the wicket of Towhid Hridoy by delivering an excellent straighter. By doing so he ended his debut innings with 2-61.
Hridoy who was forced to leave the ground yesterday with a muscle cramp returned to resume batting after Shadman's dismissal but couldn't add any runs to his 42.
After his dismissal, Bangladesh suddenly found themselves in an awkward situation by reeling at 221-5 but Liton and Mehidy Hasan Miraz looked solid in the crease, offering the side some hope.
Warrican turned one sharply to rattle the stump of Miraz, dismissing him for 15.
Shamar Joseph who ended with 2-41, dealt a double blow with the wickets of Nayeem Hasan and Hasan Murad.
Warrican came back to complete his fourth five-wicket haul by dismissing Taijul Islam and Shoriful Islam as Bangladesh lost their last five wickets for 19 runs, leaving Liton stranded on 34 at the other end.

item.title: Bayern boss Kompany out of hospital after meningeal irritation
item.description:
Bayern Munich sporting director Max Eberl said Wednesday coach Vincent Kompany had been discharged from hospital, revealing the Belgian had been suffering from meningeal irritation.
Kompany was rushed to hospital after collapsing on the training pitch in Munich on Friday, with Bayern saying the coach was suffering from a virus.
Speaking minutes before Bayern's last-32 German Cup tie with Magdeburg, Eberl told ARD the doctors had determined the cause of the illness and had discharged the 40-year-old Kompany.
"We have identified the cause: it is a case of meningeal irritation, which is what triggered the incident last Friday," Eberl said.
On Saturday, Bayern said it was a matter of "weeks, not days" until Kompany returned to the dugout, with English assistant coach Aaron Danks taking over in his absence.
After Sunday's 3-1 win at Freiburg, Danks said the coaching staff would avoid talking football with the ailing Kompany during his recovery.
"He has now been allowed to go home, where he can continue his rehabilitation," Eberl said on Wednesday.
"For him, rehabilitation means rest and medication. I am very, very confident that he will be back on the touchline at 100 percent very soon."
"I believe it is the best and most wonderful news for all of us," Eberl said.
Kompany was visibly sick and walked with a limp during Bayern's 6-1 home win over RB Leipzig in mid-October. He was in doubt for their home clash with Arsenal four days later, but took to the dugout for the 2-2 draw, two days before his training-pitch collapse.

item.title: Shadman completes third Test century, then falls
item.description:
Shadman Islam completed his third Test century in the first over of the second day against West Indies at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium on Thursday, then was out lbw to Joshua Bishop for 105 three overs later.
Resuming on 99, the left-handed opener pushed the second ball of the day to the leg side for two to reach his hundred off 220 balls.
He added only four more runs. With the fifth ball of the 77th over, Bishop pitched a good-length delivery outside off stump that came back in and struck Shadman high on the front pad as he defended on the back foot.
The umpire gave him out. Shadman spoke to his batting partner Liton Das and reviewed the decision, but UltraEdge showed no contact with the bat and ball-tracking showed the ball pitching in line, hitting in line and going on to hit middle stump. It was Bishop's first Test wicket.
Shadman's 105 came off 234 balls and included 11 fours. Bangladesh were 221 for four when he was out.
The century was Shadman's first in 17 Test innings. His previous hundred came against Zimbabwe in April 2025, and his first was also against Zimbabwe, in 2021.
Towhid Hridoy resumed his innings after Shadman's dismissal. He had retired hurt on 42 on the first day and was carried off on a stretcher.
Bangladesh ended the opening day on 213 for three in 74 overs after bad light cut play short. Shanto won the toss and chose to bat, and Bangladesh are without Mushfiqur Rahim, who injured his finger at practice on the eve of the match.

item.title: Supporting migrant workers better
item.description:
Despite the enormous contribution of migrant workers to our economy, it is a shame that Bangladesh still lacks an effective system for grading recruitment agencies, leaving prospective migrants with little reliable information about whom they can trust.
This failure, recently acknowledged by State Minister for Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment Md Nurul Haque Nur yesterday, demands our urgent attention.
Thousands of workers invest their savings, sell land, or borrow heavily to secure overseas employment. Many are subsequently confronted with excessive recruitment fees, misleading job offers, and working conditions that differ sharply from what they were promised.
It should be understood that a licence alone cannot be treated as proof that an agency is competent, ethical, or deserving of public trust.
Agencies must be rigorously evaluated across key metrics: Recruitment practices, fee transparency, complaint histories, regulatory compliance, as well as post-placement worker protection.
These assessments should also be publicly accessible, allowing prospective migrants to make informed decisions.
However, grading alone will not solve the problem. The government must strengthen monitoring, investigate complaints promptly, and impose meaningful penalties on agencies that exploit workers.
Those repeatedly found guilty of misconduct should face licence suspension or cancellation, while victims must have access to compensation and legal assistance.
Bangladesh also needs to move away from a system that prioritizes the expansion of recruitment businesses over the quality of their services.
More agencies do not necessarily mean more opportunities, particularly when weak oversight allows unscrupulous operators to thrive. What matters is having reliable agencies that connect workers with legitimate employers at reasonable costs.
Our responsibility must also extend beyond the airport. Bangladesh's diplomatic missions should provide effective support to expatriates facing wage theft, contract violations, and workplace abuse.
Migrant workers are not merely sources of remittance income; they are citizens whose labour and sacrifices deserve protection. Building a trustworthy recruitment system is therefore a fundamental obligation to the people who help sustain our economy.

item.title: Caring for the carers
item.description:
In Bangladesh, where women shoulder most household responsibilities, the International Day of Care and Support observed today should remind us that caring for others is a shared social responsibility, not an obligation that falls disproportionately on women.
Care work is among the most essential contributions to society, yet it remains among the least recognized.
Bangladesh’s first Time-Use Survey, conducted in 2021 by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), revealed that women spend roughly seven times as much time on unpaid domestic and care work as men.
Cooking, cleaning, raising children, and caring for sick or elderly family members sustain households and enable others to pursue education and employment.
Yet this labour unfortunately remains largely invisible in economic calculations, and is often dismissed as an ordinary part of being a woman.
The consequences are significant: Women who devote hours to unpaid work have less time to pursue paid employment, develop professional skills, or participate in public life. Those who work outside the home often face a second shift of domestic responsibilities, with little support or recognition.
Meanwhile, domestic workers and other care professionals frequently face low wages, insecure employment, and inadequate protection.
Encouragingly, Bangladesh has taken an important step towards recognizing this contribution through a commitment in the FY2025-26 national budget to include the economic value of women's unpaid labour in GDP calculations.
However, this recognition must lead to meaningful change. Affordable childcare, accessible support for elderly and disabled people, stronger protections for domestic workers, and policies encouraging men to share household responsibilities are essential.
The government, employers, and communities must work together to build a care system that supports both caregivers and those who need care. Families, too, must challenge the assumption that care is naturally women's work.
Care is indispensable to our economy and society, and we would do well to understand that properly valuing it -- as well as the people providing it -- is a matter of fairness, dignity, and sustainable development.

item.title: No penalty practice? No problem for City in shoot-out win
item.description:
Enzo Maresca admitted Manchester City did not practice penalties at all this season before beating Brighton & Hove Albion in a League Cup fourth round shoot-out on Wednesday.
City goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli made two penalty saves as the League Cup holders won 4-3 in the shoot-out after twice coming from behind in a 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium.
Maresca had opted against asking his players to practice penalties in training since his close-season arrival to replace Pep Guardiola.
City's lack of spot-kick preparation was no problem thanks to reserve keeper Rulli, who denied Brighton's Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight.
Mateo Kovacic did miss from the spot but Phil Foden, Enzo Fernandez, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all successful.
"To be honest, since I've been here we never practised penalties," said Maresca, whose side will host third tier Bradford City for a place in the semi-finals.
"We're very happy with the five, even Mateo. It always happens, the one that scored during the 90 minutes, and then misses the penalty."
Kovacic had cancelled out Malick Yalcouye's opener for Brighton before half-time.
Georginio Rutter restored the Seagulls' lead after the restart, but Vitor Reis diverted in a Cherki free-kick to take the match to penalties.
"I'm not sure he changed the game, but for sure he made an impact," said Maresca of Belgian winger Doku.
"This is the reason why they are there – when they start from the beginning, to try to do their best, and if they go on from the bench, to try to make an impact."
City had suffered their first Premier League defeat this season on Saturday, losing at Aston Villa to end their 100 percent start to the top-flight campaign.
It was vital for City to bounce back with a win against Brighton as they try to remain positive while awaiting the verdict in their appeal against a guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules.
If the appeal fails, City could be hit with a massive points deduction that would effectively lead to relegation.
In the midst of a pressure-packed schedule, Maresca had no regrets about his decision to rest Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol against Brighton.
"I was happy with the way we planned the game, with the rotation, and especially I was very, very, very happy with the ones that were playing," he said.

item.title: Miami stumble to draw against Cincinnati despite Suarez strike
item.description:
Lionel Messi's Inter Miami stumbled to a 2-2 draw with Cincinnati on Wednesday in an MLS game that sprang to life after half-time with four superb goals.
Miami took the lead with a Luis Suarez strike on the hour mark, but conceded two in quick succession before grabbing back a late equalizer from substitute Riquelme Fillipi to ensure the spoils were shared.
The draw was a setback in Miami's pursuit of the Eastern Conference's second seed, as the star-studded side lost ground on the New England Revolution, who beat the New York Red Bulls 3-2.
Despite the heartbreak of Fillipi's late strike, the point could prove valuable for Cincinnati, who sit on the cusp of the automatic playoff places, but are currently headed for the wild card round and could yet miss out entirely with two games remaining.
In a low-key first half, Miami controlled possession and comprehensively out-passed Cincinnati, but were unable to pierce through.
That changed in the 61st minute, as Rodrigo De Paul picked up the ball in the middle of the park, in acres of space, and played it wide to Casemiro.
The Brazilian played it first time with the outside of his boot to Suarez, lurking just inside the box.
The Uruguayan veteran took one touch, swiveled and perfectly curled the ball into the far top corner, where it crashed down and in off the crossbar.
But Cincinnati rallied, and in the 80th minute Frenchman Kenji Mboma Dem scored with another beautiful curling effort to the far post.
He picked up the ball wide right, ran at multiple defenders with a flurry of stepovers, then cut inside to score.
Just six minutes later, Cincinnati silenced Miami's Nu Stadium by taking the lead.
Defender Samuel Gidi received a pass on the edge of the box and wrapped his left foot around the ball, sending it past Dayne St. Clair.
With Messi heavily man-marked and unable to get a shot away, De Paul sprayed a wide pass to young Brazilian attacker Fillipi, who cut back to the corner of the box and bent it through two defenders and into the far side of the goal.
Both sides had even later chances to win the game, with Suarez blasting his at the goalkeeper before Evander's shot was blocked by a defender at close range as the referee waved away handball appeals.
Inter Miami play New England on Sunday, sitting two points back and needing either a win or a draw to keep their hopes of second place alive.

item.description:
Miscreants gunned down two people, including a leader of the Jatiya Sramik League, whose activities now banned, at Pushpapara cattle market in Ataikula upazila of Pabna Sadar on Thursday evening.

The deceased were Abdus Salam (56), convener of the Pabna Sadar upazila unit of the Jatiya Sramik League, and Ripon Hossain (35), his cousin's son and president of the Ataikula union unit of the Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal.

Ataikula police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Pradip Kumar confirmed the incident to Prothom Alo.

Abdus Salam was a resident of Dharmagram in Ataikula union of Pabna Sadar. He was the leaseholder of Pushpapara cattle market.

Pradip Kumar, general secretary of the Pabna district unit of the Jatiya Sramik League, told Prothom Alo that Abdus Salam was the convener of the Sramik League's Sadar upazila unit.

However, after the political changeover on 5 August 2024, he used to post photographs on social media showing himself with leaders of other political parties.

Meanwhile, Abdul Gafur, president of the Pabna district unit of the Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, said Ripon Hossain was the president of the organisation's Ataikula union unit.

Speaking to witnesses, it was learnt that Abdus Salam and his nephew Ripon were at their office at Pushpapara market. Around 6:45pm, a group of assailants arrived and opened indiscriminate fire at them. Locals rescued the two in critical condition and took them to Pabna General Hospital, where doctors declared them dead.

OC Pradip Kumar said police were sent to the scene after receiving information about the incident. The bodies were recovered and arrangements were being made for autopsies. Several police teams have started investigating the incident.

Pabna Superintendent of Police Abu Ashraf told Prothom Alo that the killing might have been linked to a dispute over the market lease or a conflict among extremists. The police are investigating the incident, keeping both possibilities in mind.

item.title: What Tahsif said about Hasina’s August 5 helicopter video
item.description:
Former Bangladesh Air Force Flight Lieutenant Tahsif Souri, whose body was recovered from the Turag River this week, had questioned allegations that he recorded and circulated a video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country on August 5, 2024.
In an interview with YouTube-based podcast and talk show platform "Speak with Rashid" on July 21, 2026, Tahsif questioned the evidence behind the allegations and suggested they might have led to his dismissal from the Air Force.
The interview, hosted by Mamunur Rashid, has resurfaced following the recovery of his body.
During the interview, the host referred to a media report alleging that footage of Sheikh Hasina leaving the country had been recorded at Kurmitola Airport and circulated by Tahsif. The report also reportedly linked him to an investigation into the alleged involvement of India's intelligence agency, the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), within the Air Force.
Responding to the allegations, Tahsif said the report had claimed that Rifat Ashrafi recorded the video and that he had circulated it. He questioned what evidence supported the allegation that he had shared the footage.
“Even if I recorded the video or circulated it, what proof do they have? I want to ask that,” he said.
Asked whether the allegations had led to his dismissal from the Air Force, Tahsif said this was possible but declined to disclose details of the events at the time.
“I cannot disclose everything, and there are things I am unable to discuss. I think they did this because of these allegations,” he said.
Tahsif also said he faced social embarrassment and harassment after the report was published, claiming its headline and presentation had created a misleading impression of him among readers.
He rejected the allegations of RAW's involvement within the Air Force, saying: “If I were linked to RAW, why would I be in Bangladesh? If I were linked to RAW, why would I speak publicly?”
He described the allegation as “a very ridiculous claim”.
Tahsif further claimed that the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) directorate had said he had no such involvement. However, no detailed documents supporting the claim were presented during the interview.
Asked whether he had appealed against his discharge from the Air Force, Tahsif said he had not and was uncertain whether he would do so in the future.
He also expressed frustration over the withholding of his passport, describing it as a violation of his democratic rights.
“They had withheld my passport, which is my democratic right. I am deeply upset about this. I suffered for two years,” he said, adding that he had since recovered the passport.
Tahsif's father, KM Enayetul Karim Helal, told journalists at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital on Thursday that his son had been dismissed from the Air Force in September 2024, following the change of government the previous month.
He said the family had been told that the dismissal was related to disciplinary issues.
“Only the department can explain this. The department simply told us that it is a disciplined organisation and that he was discharged because of indiscipline,” he said.
After leaving the Air Force, Tahsif worked at the Bangladesh Cricket Board and Netra News. Most recently, he was employed as an administration and security officer at Vargo Tobacco.
Asked whether his son had received any threats, his father said Tahsif occasionally told him that he felt apprehensive. However, he said he did not know what had caused his son's concerns and clarified that Tahsif had never told him he had been threatened.
His father also said the family had no information about whether Tahsif had recorded or circulated the video of Sheikh Hasina leaving the country.
“We know nothing about this matter, or even whether he actually posted the video,” he said.
Tahsif's body was recovered from the Turag River on Wednesday and sent to the morgue at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.
After the autopsy, Dr Nashat Jabin, head of the hospital's forensic medicine department and an assistant professor, said samples from Tahsif's liver, kidneys, stomach and blood had been collected and sent for testing. Samples for DNA profiling were also collected.
The cause of death will be established after the test results are received, she said.
Dhaka District River Police Superintendent Abdullah Al Mamun said on Thursday that no externally visible injuries or wounds had been found on Tahsif's body.
He said the cause of death would be determined after the autopsy report was received, adding that further legal action would be taken based on complaints from the family.

item.title: Who is Deep, the friend who last met Tahsif before his death
item.description:
Ahmed Shahriar Reza Deep, a friend of former Bangladesh Air Force flight lieutenant Tahsif Souri, has come into the spotlight following Tahsif’s death.
On October 27, Deep left home with Tahsif. The two repaired Tahsif’s motorcycle and later had dinner before parting ways in the House Building area of Uttara.
Deep said that after returning home, he called Tahsif but found his phone switched off. He was also unable to reach him by phone the following morning.
Speaking to journalists on Thursday, Deep discussed his relationship with Tahsif, the events of that day and their business dealings. Deep said he had known Tahsif for around 6 years. He described Tahsif as an elder brother and said he addressed him as such because Tahsif was older.
Deep recently graduated in civil engineering from the Islamic University of Technology (IUT) and currently lives in Mohammadpur, Dhaka.
According to Deep, Tahsif’s motorcycle had broken down and would not start. As Deep had some knowledge of motorcycles, Tahsif sought his advice. Deep subsequently went to Tahsif’s home, and the two tried for around 10 to 20 minutes before getting the motorcycle started. They then took it to a workshop for necessary repairs and an oil change.
After the work was completed, Tahsif invited Deep to dinner. They later ate together at a restaurant in Rupayan Shopping Complex in Uttara.
Deep said they left after dinner on separate motorcycles. When they reached the House Building area of Uttara, he went in one direction while Tahsif headed in another. He said they parted ways at around midnight.
Deep said he had noticed nothing unusual about Tahsif’s behavior that day. He recalled that one of Tahsif’s friends had called him while they were eating, but their conversation appeared normal.
Deep said he called Tahsif after reaching home but found his phone switched off. Tahsif had been charging his phone using a power bank at the restaurant. Deep therefore assumed that the phone had run out of charge and switched off. He tried calling again the following morning but could not reach him.
Asked whether he suspected anyone in connection with Tahsif’s disappearance, Deep said he had no reason to suspect anyone at that point. He said there had been no conversation with Tahsif since they first met that could have led him to anticipate an incident.
Deep said: “Like the other 10 people, I am in exactly the same mystery.”
Tahsif’s father, KM Enayetul Karim Helal, had said that his son had recently started a security guard supply business and that Deep looked after the work.
Deep also acknowledged having a business connection with Tahsif. According to him, personal disagreements could arise among acquaintances over business matters, but the issue was not particularly serious.
Deep was also acquainted with members of Tahsif’s family. Tahsif’s father said Deep’s parents had visited the family’s home once.
Deep said Tahsif would occasionally tell him to look after his younger brother if anything happened to him. However, he did not want to elaborate on why Tahsif made such remarks.
Regarding a viral video of Tahsif concerning former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s departure from the country, Deep said he had learned about it through the media. He said he had not discussed the matter with Tahsif.
He said he had gone to the morgue when Tahsif’s body was taken away following the autopsy. He added that he had not gone out since then, out of consideration for the concerns of Tahsif’s family.
According to Deep, he and Tahsif parted ways after dinner on the night of October 27, and he had no further contact with Tahsif. However, he said he had no information about what exactly happened that night.

item.title: Technical glitch fixed; Biman flight carrying PM expected to leave Tokyo for Dhaka shortly
item.description:
The technical glitch on the Biman Bangladesh Airlines aircraft that delayed Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s flight to Dhaka from Tokyo was fixed on Thursday night, and the flight is expected to leave Narita International Airport shortly.
Captain Md Imamul Islam announced around 9:50pm local time that the problem was resolved and that passengers would start boarding the aircraft again soon.
The Biman flight was scheduled to leave Tokyo at 6pm local time.
The aircraft left its terminal around 6:18pm and moved to the runway for takeoff.
However, it stopped before taking off, and about 15 minutes later, the captain announced that the flight could not proceed due to a technical problem.
He said two engineers were working to resolve the issue. The aircraft was later taken back to the tarmac, and all passengers disembarked.
Around 8pm local time, the captain announced that it would take another two and a half hours to fix the problem.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and other members of his entourage were on board the aircraft.
The flight was originally scheduled to arrive at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 10:35pm Bangladesh time.
