item.title: Swapan: Misinterpretation of religion, patriarchal mindsets hinder women's empowerment
item.description:
Misinterpretation of religion and patriarchal attitudes remain major challenges to gender equality and women's empowerment in Bangladesh, Prime Minister's Political Adviser Zahir Uddin Swapan said on Thursday.
“Misinterpretation of religion and patriarchal attitudes remain major challenges to achieving gender equality and ensuring women’s empowerment in Bangladesh. These challenges must be addressed if we are to build an equitable, inclusive and developed Bangladesh. Alongside reducing existing inequalities between women and men, it is essential to ensure equal opportunities for women in education, employment, leadership and decision-making,” he said.
Swapan made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the 'IDG Carnival 2026', organised by Save the Children in Bangladesh at a hotel in the capital to mark the International Day of the Girl.
He stressed the need to address these challenges and ensure equal opportunities for women in education, employment, leadership and decision-making to build an equitable, inclusive and developed Bangladesh.
Held under the theme "Rooted in Every Region, Advancing Every Adolescent Girl", the event brought together policymakers, development partners, youth representatives and other stakeholders to promote the rights, leadership and meaningful participation of girls and adolescent girls in society.
The prime minister's adviser said the government placed particular importance on gender equality and women's empowerment as part of its vision for building the Bangladesh of the future.
However, achieving these goals required effective contributions from both the government and development partners, he said.
"Save the Children's experience, support and partnerships can make an important contribution in this regard," Swapan said, expressing hope that the organisation would continue working with the government to advance women's rights, eliminate discrimination and build a more equitable society.
Dr Md Saimum Parvez, special assistant to the prime minister on environment, forest and climate change, attended the event as the guest of honour.
Members of Parliament Helen Zerin Khan, Mahmuda Habiba and Mansura Akter attended as special guests, while Dr Eliza Azei, head of the Adolescents and Youth Programme at UNFPA Bangladesh, was also present.
Discussions at the carnival highlighted the need to remove barriers that prevent girls and adolescent girls from accessing education, employment, leadership opportunities, entrepreneurship and decision-making processes.
The government places particular importance on gender equality and women’s empowerment as part of its vision for building the Bangladesh of the future, said the PM's Adviser.
However, achieving this goal requires effective contributions not only from the government but also from development partners.
The event highlighted the importance of creating opportunities for girls and adolescent girls to realise their potential, develop leadership skills and participate actively in decision-making processes.
Dr. Md. Saimum Parvez, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Environment, Forest and Climate Change, attended the event as the Guest of Honour.
Members of Parliament Helen Zerin Khan, Mahmuda Habiba and Mansura Akter attended as Special Guests.
Dr. Eliza Azei, Head of Adolescents and Youth Programme at the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) Bangladesh, was also present.
Speakers also stressed the importance of coordinated efforts by families, communities, the government, development partners and other institutions to create safe, inclusive and supportive environments where the voices, experiences and needs of girls and adolescent girls are recognised and valued.
Organised under Save the Children in Bangladesh’s SWOCCHAR project, the initiative served as an important platform for strengthening collective efforts to promote the rights and empowerment of girls and adolescent girls.
Participants expressed their expectation that creating equal opportunities for adolescent girls, amplifying their voices and increasing their participation in policymaking and decision-making processes will contribute to building a more equitable and inclusive society.

item.title: Thakurgaon-1 by-election ends, vote counting begins
item.description:
Polling in the Thakurgaon-1 by-election concluded without any reported violence or disorder on Thursday, with voting ending at around 4:30pm after starting at 8am.
The constituency covers Thakurgaon Sadar, Ruhia and Bhulli. Vote counting began immediately after polling ended.
Voter turnout was relatively low in the morning but increased toward noon, according to observations at several polling centers across the constituency. Reports from different centers indicated that around 50-60% of votes had been cast by noon.
At Krishnapur Government Primary School polling center in Ward 8 of Rahimnagar Union, presiding officer Saiful Islam said around 40% of votes had been cast by 12:30pm.
Voters Farazul Islam of Paikpara village and Farhad Hossain of Prostampur village said they had cast their ballots in a peaceful environment and described voter turnout as good.
At Polling Centre No 112 at Raipur Government Primary School in Election Area 3 of Thakurgaon Sadar upazila, around 55% of votes had been cast by 1:30pm.
Promila, a voter from the Raipur area, said she had come to vote with her husband, while her son and daughter-in-law had voted in the morning. Another voter from the same area, Madhai Chandra, also arrived with his wife to cast his ballot.
However, Abdul Latif, a voter from Gobindanagar, said he faced difficulties at Thakurgaon Government Polytechnic Institute while helping his ailing wife, Sharifa Begum, cast her vote.
He said he struggled to take her to the second floor and argued that polling booths for sick voters and people with mobility difficulties should not have been placed there.
A mobile court fined Abdul Karim, president of the Jamaat-e-Islami Ward 1 unit in Jagannathpur Union of Thakurgaon Sadar upazila, Tk5,000 for allegedly distributing leaflets at JP School polling center in the Jagannathpur area around noon.
He faces 1 month of simple imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine.
Meanwhile, law enforcement agencies detained 3 alleged fake voters at Danarhat Ansaria Fazil Madrasa polling center in Thakurgaon Sadar around noon on Thursday.
The detainees were identified as Himel and Siam, second-year students of the Alim program, and Minhaj, a first-year Alim student at the madrasa.
A total of 516,138 voters are eligible to vote in the by-election, which is being held at 185 polling centers across Thakurgaon Sadar, Ruhia and Bhulli, with 989 polling booths.
Five candidates are contesting the seat: BNP's Mirza Faisal Amin; Md Delawar Hossain, backed by the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami; Hafez Dr Md Khademul Islam of Islami Andolan Bangladesh; Md Abdul Alim Nizami of Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan; and Husain Muhammad Omar Faruk of Bangladesh Congress.
Extensive security measures have been deployed by law enforcement agencies and the administration. Around 5,300 law enforcement personnel are on duty, and closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras have been installed at all polling centers.
BNP candidate Mirza Faisal Amin said voting was taking place in a festive atmosphere.
“Undoubtedly, voting is taking place in a festive atmosphere. Every voter is my voter. All voters in this area want to cast their votes peacefully. Despite this being a by-election, a large turnout has been observed. I still believe that the voters' opinions are final,” he said.
Md Delawar Hossain, the candidate backed by the 11-party alliance, said the election's credibility depended on the government and those responsible for conducting it, as the vote was being held under a party-led government.
“Since this election is being held under a party-led government, it depends entirely on the government and those responsible for conducting the election. If the government, administration and election officials act sincerely, they can deliver a free and fair election. If they fail, the public will lose confidence in future local elections and other elections held under party-led governments, and people will lose interest in elections,” he said.
Thakurgaon Superintendent of Police Belal Hossain said voting began peacefully at all 185 polling centers at 8am.
He said all centers were being monitored through online body-worn cameras and equipped with CCTV cameras, adding that polling had proceeded peacefully across the constituency.

item.title: Gas emerges from submersible pump in Gopalganj, ignites into flames
item.description:
Gas emerging from a submersible pump in Gopalganj’s Kotalipara upazila has caught fire when exposed to a lighter, prompting locals to call for an expert investigation.
The incident occurred at Bhashai Bazar in Bandhabari union, where hardware trader Kamrul Sheikh installed the pump about a year ago to supply water to fish transport vehicles.
Kamrul said the pump had been producing less water over the past week. Out of curiosity, he held a gas lighter near the pipe’s opening on Wednesday night, and flames erupted.
News of the incident quickly spread, drawing crowds to his shop on Thursday. At the request of curious onlookers, Kamrul repeatedly demonstrated how the gas caught fire when a lighter was brought near the pipe.
The residents urged the authorities to send a team of experts to determine whether natural gas was present underground.
Kamrul, son of Rob Sheikh, said he had installed the pump at a depth of 280 feet to supply water to fish transport vehicles.
Local youth Shihab Sheikh said he visited the site on Thursday morning after hearing about the incident the previous night.
“We witnessed the phenomenon ourselves. We want a team of experts to examine the site and determine whether there is really gas underground. If gas is found here, it could benefit the country,” he said.
Kotalipara Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Saif-ul-Arefin said he had sent local land officials to the site after learning about the incident.
“Based on their initial report, I have received confirmation of the incident. I will visit the site on Friday and decide on the next steps,” he said.

item.title: Dr Zahed: Youth should help seniors identify fake news
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting and Cultural Affairs Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman has urged young people to help senior citizens develop media and information literacy skills to identify fake news and misinformation.
He made the call as the chief guest at a seminar titled “Media and Information Literacy Skills for 21st Century Youth” and a special award ceremony at the Manzur Elahi Auditorium of East West University (EWU) on October 29, 2026.
Addressing the gathering, Zahed said fake news and misinformation were spreading rapidly in Bangladesh, as in the rest of the world. He said the government prioritized educating and empowering citizens over imposing strict regulatory controls.
He also noted that older adults were often more vulnerable to misinformation on social media than younger people, urging the youth to help seniors identify inauthentic information.
The event was organized by EWU's Department of Information Studies as part of the nationwide celebration of Global Media and Information Literacy (MIL) Week 2026. It was held in collaboration with the UNESCO Dhaka Office, the Media and Information Literacy Network Bangladesh (MILNetBD), and the UN Electoral Project “Ballot.”
Professor Dr Mohammed Farashuddin, chairperson of EWU's Board of Trustees, chaired the seminar.
Professor Dr M Ashik Mosaddik, acting vice-chancellor of EWU; Dr Susan Vize, UNESCO representative to Bangladesh; and Andrés del Castillo Sánchez, representative of the UN Electoral Project “Ballot” Bangladesh, attended as special guests.
Professor Dr Dilara Begum, chairperson of EWU's Department of Information Studies, presented the keynote paper, which was discussed by Professor Dr Kazi Mostak Gausul Hoq of the Department of Information Science and Library Management at the University of Dhaka.
Following the seminar, awards were presented to students and awareness advocates in recognition of their contributions to the week-long media literacy activities.

item.title: Five of a family burned in Gazipur gas leak fire
item.description:
Five members of a family suffered burn injuries in a fire caused by a gas leak in Kashimpur, Gazipur, on Thursday morning.
The victims were taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka for treatment around 2pm.
The fire broke out in the Sardagong area of Kashimpur at around 8:30am on Thursday.
The injured were identified as Arifa Begum, Faria, Rozina, 18, child Rahim and Riazul Sheikh.
Riazul suffered burns to 40% of his body, while Arifa sustained burns to 5%, Faria to 8%, and Rozina and one-year-old Rahim to less than 1% each. Riazul's condition is critical.
Talha Bin Jasim, an official at the Fire Service and Civil Defence media cell, said, quoting Dr Sultan Mahmud Shikder, resident surgeon (emergency) at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, that all five victims were receiving necessary treatment and remained under observation.

item.title: Rizvi: Thakurgaon-1 by-election held peacefully
item.description:
BNP acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Thursday said voting in the by-election to Thakurgaon-1 constituency was peaceful, with no reports of polling-centre occupation, vote rigging or clashes.
He said the BNP is optimistic about the election, citing satisfactory voter turnout and a favourable electoral environment.
Rizvi made the remarks while talking to reporters at the BNP’s central office in Nayapaltan in the afternoon.
“Since morning, we have seen people casting their votes in an excellent and peaceful environment,” he said.
The BNP leader said his party is optimistic about the election as voting took place in a fair environment with satisfactory voter turnout.
He also urged opposition parties not to make baseless allegations about the election.

item.title: Former Awami League leader found dead in Chittagong
item.description:
Police recovered the body of Nur Nahar Begum, 74, a former Awami League leader, from her home in Chittagong’s East Madarbari area on Wednesday evening.
No visible injury marks were found on her body, but two mobile phones she used were missing, police said. Nur Nahar had been suffering from cancer for a long time.
Nur Nahar was the former women’s affairs secretary of East Madarbari ward unit of the Awami League.
According to local sources, her eldest son recently died of blood cancer. She had since been living with her younger son. On Wednesday morning, her son left for work, while her pregnant daughter-in-law was at her parental home, leaving Nur Nahar alone in the house.
Sadarghat police station Officer-in-Charge Ekram Ullah told Dhaka Tribune that tenants noticed the house’s back door open in the evening. They entered and found her dead on her bed.
Police recovered the body and collected evidence from the scene.
The OC said family members reported that Nur Nahar suffered from cancer, diabetes, high blood pressure and other health complications. Although no visible injury marks were found, police are investigating the death. The cause will be confirmed after the autopsy report is received, he added.

item.title: BNP’s Faisal Amin scores landslide win in Thakurgaon-1
item.description:
BNP-nominated candidate Mirza Faisal Amin has unofficially won the Thakurgaon-1 by-election by a landslide, securing 227,789 votes, more than twice the 96,453 votes received by his closest rival Jamaat-e-Islami candidate Delwar Hossain.
According to the results from all 185 polling centres, Faisal Amin won by a margin of 131,336 votes.
Returning Officer and District Election Officer Kamrul Islam declared Faisal Amin the unofficial winner at around 8:45pm on Thursday.
Voting began at 8:00am across all 185 polling centres and continued until 4pm, followed by vote counting.
According to the district election office, the constituency has 516,138 registered voters, of whom 64.77% cast their ballots.
Five candidates contested the by-election. They were Mirza Faisal Amin of the BNP, contesting with the sheaf of paddy symbol; Delwar Hossain of Jamaat-e-Islami, with the scales symbol; Md Abdul Alim Nizami of Bangladesh Khelafat Andolon, with the banyan tree symbol; Md Khademul Islam of Islami Andolan Bangladesh, with the hand fan symbol; and Husain Muhammad Omar Faruk of Bangladesh Congress, with the coconut symbol.

item.title: Home Minister urges police to serve people with professionalism, neutrality
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Thursday urged police officers to build a truly people-oriented police force through professionalism, neutrality and humane behaviour.
“Police must earn public trust by standing beside people, serving them and working for their welfare. They must win people's hearts through their service,” he said while addressing the basic training completion parade of the 27th Trainee Sergeants and 43rd Cadet Sub-Inspectors (2006 batch) at the parade ground of Bangladesh Police Academy at Sarda in Rajshahi.
He said people have high expectations of the police and called on officers to provide sincere services to people from all walks of life. Police must deliver legal services and protection without fear or favouritism, he said, stressing the need to establish themselves as a force that genuinely serves people.
Addressing the newly trained officers, Salahuddin said the members of the batch joined the profession of public service after nearly two decades of waiting, legal proceedings and various challenges.
Urging them to learn from past experiences, he instructed the officers not to practise discrimination or injustice in their professional or personal lives. He called on them to view their uniforms and assigned duties not merely as a job but as a solemn commitment to public safety, justice and the maintenance of law and order.
The minister also urged police to replace misconduct, bias and the use of muscle power with professionalism, competence and humane policing.
Inspector General of Police Md Ali Hossain Fakir, Bangladesh Police Academy Principal Md Mainul Hasan BPM, Rajshahi Divisional Commissioner (in charge) Md Rezaul Alam Sarker and Rajshahi Range DIG Md Ashik Sayeed attended the programme as special guests.
The minister inspected the parade, received the salute and distributed awards among trainees who excelled in different categories.
Among the 27th trainee sergeants, Mohammad Omar Faruk received the Best Sergeant award, Mohammad Delwar Hossain was named Best in Academics, Saiful Islam received the Best in Field Activities award, and Md Asaduzzaman was recognised as Best Shooter.
From the 43rd Cadet Sub-Inspector (2006 batch), Mohammad Jahangir Alam was named Best Cadet, Md Borhanul Islam received the Best in Academics award, Dewan Golam Rasul was recognised as Best in Field Activities, and Md Kamal Gani received the Best Shooter award.

item.title: KUET dismisses five teachers, two employees
item.description:
Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET) has dismissed five teachers and two employees following investigations into allegations of recruitment irregularities, violations of university rules and submission of false documents.
The decision was taken at the university's 115th syndicate meeting, KUET Registrar Engineer Md Anichur Rahman Bhuiyan said on Thursday.
The dismissed teachers are Professor Dr Pintu Chandra Shil of the Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) department, Professor Dr Subrata Talapatra of the Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM) department, Assistant Professor Nibir Mondal of the Energy Science and Engineering (ESE) department, Professor Dr Masrura Mostafa and Assistant Professor Shahriar Roman of the Humanities and Business department.
The other two are Deputy Registrar Nimai Chandra Mistry and office assistant Satyajit Kumar Dutta.
All seven had been under temporary suspension for an extended period.
According to university sources, allegations against Pintu Chandra Shil emerged following the 2024 mass uprising, leading to his suspension. During the suspension period, he allegedly failed to attend the campus regularly. His name was also found on the websites of two private universities, although KUET had not authorised him to work there. These allegations were among the grounds for his dismissal.
Subrata Talapatra joined KUET as a lecturer on October 20, 2010. An investigation found that he was over 30 when he applied for the position, exceeding the age limit under the university's recruitment rules.
Masrura Mostafa was also reportedly over 30 when she applied for the post of lecturer. She was later promoted to assistant professor by counting her experience at a private university, which the authorities deemed inconsistent with KUET's regulations.
Shahriar Roman allegedly failed to meet the academic requirements for appointment as a lecturer, which stipulated first-class results in both honours and master's examinations. He had obtained second-class results in both degrees. The investigation also found that two research papers cited in his application for the post of assistant professor did not exist.
Nibir Mondal cited experience gained through project-based employment when joining KUET, which was not recognised under the university's recruitment rules, according to the findings. While under suspension, he travelled abroad with the authorities' permission but failed to return and rejoin his workplace within the stipulated period.
Mistry was accused of submitting false experience documents when applying for the post of section officer at KUET, while Dutta allegedly secured his job by understating his age on his national identity card.
Mistry and Mondal reportedly filed writ petitions with the High Court challenging their suspensions.
However, the KUET registrar's office said the university had handled the cases in accordance with the law. It said the petitions concerned the legality of keeping employees suspended for more than six months, rather than the specific allegations against them.
Registrar Anichur Rahman Bhuiyan said the syndicate had decided to dismiss the seven employees after reviewing the allegations and seeking explanations from several of them.
"There were allegations against them, which led to their temporary suspension. After investigating the allegations, the university sought explanations from several of them," he said.

item.title: Spinners strike between rain and bad light as West Indies reach 134-4 in Mirpur
item.description:
Bangladesh’s spinners took three wickets in quick succession after a rain and bad-light interruption, but bad light brought the second day of the first Test to an early close with the West Indies on 134 for four on Thursday.
West Indies trail Bangladesh's first-innings total of 272 by 138 runs. Tagenarine Chanderpaul was unbeaten on 43 and Justin Greaves on 15 at stumps.
Only 71.4 overs were bowled on Thursday at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium, after 74 on the opening day.
Bad light forced an early tea with West Indies on 89 for one in 27 overs, and rain began during the break. About an hour was lost before the third session started.
Bangladesh struck soon after the restart. Mehidy Hasan Miraz had opener John Campbell caught at slip by captain Najmul Hossain Shanto for 54, with West Indies on 95.
Left-arm spinner Taijul Islam then took two wickets in a wicket maiden in the 36th over. Kavem Hodge was caught at silly point for seven off the first ball, and Amir Jangoo was caught by Tanzid Hasan attempting a slog sweep off the fifth, leaving West Indies on 97 for four.
Chanderpaul and Greaves added 37 before the umpires checked their light meters and took the players off again. No further play was possible.
Campbell had been dropped twice before reaching his sixth Test fifty, his third in a row. Hasan Mahmud removed Brandon King for 15 in the fifth over of the innings.
Earlier, Bangladesh lost their last seven wickets for 59 runs. Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican took five for 53 after Shadman Islam completed his third Test century in the first over of the day and was out for 105 soon after.
Wicketkeeper Litton Kumer Das did not take the field after being hit on the right elbow while batting. Team physio Bayjedul Islam Khan said Liton's elbow was bruised and he was under observation, with Jaker Ali keeping wicket as a substitute.

item.title: Thakurgaon-1 by-election: Jamaat, BNP trade accusations over campaign
item.description:
Candidates from Jamaat-e-Islami and the BNP have traded accusations over the electoral environment ahead of the Thakurgaon-1 by-election, with Jamaat candidate Delawar Hossain alleging campaign obstruction and voter intimidation, while BNP candidate Mirza Faisal Amin dismissed the claims as fabricated attempts to undermine the election.
Despite the allegations, Delawar said he would remain in the race, while Mirza Faisal Amin pledged to accept the election results, whatever the outcome.
Speaking at a press conference at a restaurant in Thakurgaon town on Wednesday evening, Delawar said his party intended to contest the election until the end and remained confident in the election preparations and the administration’s role.
However, he warned that if the situation resembled the 1994 Magura by-election, his party would take necessary measures depending on the circumstances.
Delawar alleged that his party’s campaign was being obstructed, activists were being attacked, and voters were being intimidated at their homes. He also accused government officials and employees of being used for partisan electoral activities.
He expressed concern over whether voters would be able to reach polling stations without hindrance.
Delawar also raised concerns about voter turnout, suggesting that people living outside Dhaka might be less inclined to travel to vote in a by-election. He said the reported threats and intimidation had added to uncertainty surrounding the polls.
Responding to the BNP’s allegation that there was a plan to prevent minority voters from reaching polling stations, Delawar dismissed the claim as false and baseless. He said all citizens, regardless of religion or background, had the right to vote safely and urged Hindu voters and other members of the community to go to polling stations without fear.
At a separate press conference at the district BNP office on Wednesday night, Mirza Faisal Amin rejected Jamaat’s allegations, saying false claims were being used to create controversy and undermine confidence in the election.
He alleged that leaders and activists of the 11-party alliance were attempting to confuse voters through a series of accusations, some of which, he claimed, had already been disproved by the relevant authorities.
Mirza Faisal Amin said allegations of attacks, threats and other irregularities were being used to generate controversy. He also denied allegations that the BNP was distributing money to voters, describing the claims as baseless and unsupported by evidence.
In contrast, he alleged that there was substantial evidence of Jamaat distributing money.
On whether he would accept the election results, Mirza Faisal Amin said he would respect the outcome, arguing that rejecting the results would amount to a lack of faith in democratic principles. He said democracy required respect for the people’s will.
Delawar described the election as a test of whether public confidence in the electoral system could be restored. He said a free, fair and impartial election was possible even under a partisan government and urged the administration to set an example through the voting process.
The competing allegations have put the electoral environment and voter safety at the centre of discussion ahead of the by-election. Ensuring that voters can reach polling stations without pressure or intimidation remains a key concern, alongside the need for the results to reflect the electorate’s choice.
Party leaders and activists attended both press conferences.

item.title: ISU welcomes Fall 2026 semester students
item.description:
International Standard University (ISU) organized a freshers’ reception for students of the Fall 2026 semester at its Mohakhali campus auditorium on Thursday, featuring speeches by university officials and cultural performances by students.
The program was held under the chairmanship of ISU Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Abdul Awal Khan. Member Secretary of the Board of Trustees Hasnat Mosharraf attended as the special guest.
Abdul Awal Khan said the university aims to develop skilled and humane individuals through quality education and research. He urged students to uphold honesty, ethics, and human values alongside academic and professional success.
He also emphasized the importance of acquiring relevant skills in a technology-driven world and reaffirmed the university’s commitment to academic excellence, research quality, establishing a permanent campus, and holding its convocation.
Addressing the new students, Hasnat Mosharraf said ISU aims to prepare students for professional success while enabling them to contribute positively to society. He highlighted the importance of technological knowledge, creativity, and lifelong learning in navigating a changing world.
He also encouraged students to develop leadership qualities through mutual trust, honesty, and cooperation, noting that success lies in empowering others and creating new opportunities.
During the event, the newcomers were welcomed with flowers and introduced to the university’s academic programs, facilities, and co-curricular opportunities. Students from different departments performed music, dance, and group presentations as part of the cultural segment.

item.title: How to check HSC results 2026?
item.description:
The results of the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) 2026 and equivalent examinations will be published at 11am on Saturday.
Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon will inaugurate the result publication at the conference room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division at the Ministry of Education.
The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee announced the schedule.
According to the release, results will be published simultaneously on the websites of the respective education boards and educational institutions as soon as the announcement begins.
Educational institutions can download the results from eduboardresults.gov.bd and educationboardresults.gov.bd. Students can also check their results on these websites and the websites of their respective education boards, or collect them from their institutions.
Students can check their results by typing HSC, followed by a space, the first three letters of their education board's name, another space, their roll number and the examination year, and sending the message to 16140.
For example, students have to send HSC DHA 123456 2026 to 16140.
Students can apply online for re-scrutiny of their answer scripts from November 1 to 7.
The application process and relevant instructions will be published on the websites of the respective education boards.
The press release said results would not be available directly from the education boards, the Ministry of Education or newspaper offices.

item.title: Liberation DocFest opens in Dhaka with 17 Films
item.description:
The 13th edition of Liberation DocFest Bangladesh begins in Dhaka on Thursday, featuring 17 documentary films from Bangladesh and other countries under the theme “Presence in Absence”.
The three-day festival, running until October 31, will take place at the Liberation War Museum in Agargaon and Alliance Française de Dhaka in Dhanmondi. The programme includes screenings, seminars and discussions focusing on documentary cinema, freedom and human rights.
This year’s programme features National and International Competition sections, alongside a “Best of the Fest” category.
According to the organisers, 188 films were submitted from different countries, with 18 selected by an 8-member preview committee. The organisers said the festival aims to promote documentary filmmaking on freedom and human rights, strengthen ties between local and international filmmakers, and encourage younger generations to explore the genre.
The selected films explore themes including gender equality, resistance, displacement, statelessness, generational memory, ecological crises, ancestral roots and the legacy of Bangladesh’s Liberation War.
The winning film in each of the National and International Competition sections will receive Tk100,000. A nine-member Youth Jury will also select a film, whose makers will receive a crest and certificate.
The National Competition jury comprises filmmaker Shabnam Ferdousi, visual artist and filmmaker Dilara Begum, and Sajjad Hossain, a teacher at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh.
The International Competition jury includes cultural personality M Hamid, filmmaker Shameem Akhtar and human rights activist Asif Munier.
A seminar on connecting younger generations with the history and memory of the Liberation War will be held at 4pm on October 30 at the Liberation War Museum. The discussion will examine opportunities and challenges in incorporating documentary filmmaking into higher education assignments.
Launched in 2006, Liberation DocFest Bangladesh has provided a platform for filmmakers to explore freedom, human dignity and human rights through documentary cinema.

item.title: Farooki rejects separation reports, focuses on upcoming films
item.description:
Filmmaker Mostofa Sarwar Farooki has dismissed reports of a possible separation from actress Nusrat Imrose Tisha, describing the claims about their marriage as false.
Speculation about the couple’s relationship intensified after several media outlets reported that they were allegedly living separately. Farooki said neither he nor Tisha would comment on the reports, arguing that doing so would give further attention to the claims.
He said he was focusing on upcoming projects instead of responding to what he described as personal attacks and misinformation.
Farooki also shared updates on his recent work, saying he travelled to South Korea on October 10 at the invitation of the Busan International Film Festival, where he delivered a speech on film.
Before leaving for Busan, he completed work on an advertisement. After returning to Bangladesh on October 17, he began working on another commercial project.
The filmmaker said he had completed the story for one film and started developing another. He is also working on three advertisements, including one for a healthcare company and two for building materials.
According to Farooki, one of the advertisements has already been filmed in Dhaka, Mymensingh and South Korea.
Meanwhile, Tisha has continued her professional activities amid the speculation. She recently launched her production company, Fullscreen, which released a drama starring Arsh Khan and Priyanti Urbi on its YouTube channel on September 28.
Farooki also said Tisha was in discussions to act in a new international film but declined to share further details, adding that an announcement would be made once arrangements were finalised.
Farooki and Tisha married on July 16, 2010, after a five-year relationship that began when they met through their work in the entertainment industry. Their daughter, Ilham Nusrat Farooki, was born in 2022.

item.title: Zainine Karim wins best actor at IFFSA Toronto
item.description:
Bangladeshi actress Zainine Karim Chowdhury has won the Best Actor (International Feature) award at the 2026 International Film Festival of South Asia (IFFSA) Toronto for her performance in The Difficult Bride , directed by Rubaiyat Hossain and produced by Khona Talkies.
Held in Toronto from October 8 to 18, the festival is part of the South Asian Screen Council of Canada, one of North America’s major platforms for South Asian cinema.
In The Difficult Bride , Zainine portrays a woman caught between family expectations, personal desires and control over her own body. The festival jury praised the fearlessness and physical intensity of her performance.
The jury also commended her transitions between vulnerability, suppressed anger and defiance, noting that her portrayal anchors the film’s exploration of womanhood, oppression and resistance.
The award adds to the film’s festival achievements this year. The Difficult Bride has previously screened at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, the BFI London Film Festival and the Toronto International Film Festival.
Set in a traditional beauty parlour in Dhaka, the film follows a bride-to-be who grows increasingly frustrated with the grooming and makeover rituals arranged by her family. As the pressure mounts, she begins to resist the expectations imposed on her.
The cast includes Rikita Nandini Shimu, Sunerah Binte Kamal, Azmeri Haque Badhon, Damer Khan, Shatabdi Wadud, Saberi Alam and Mohammad Bari, alongside Zainine.

item.title: Flimmaker Jafar Panahi receives prison sentence in Iran
item.description:
Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi has been sentenced to five years and one month in prison by a Tehran Revolutionary Court in a separate verdict, according to his lawyer.
The filmmaker, who was previously sentenced to one year in prison, has also been barred from travelling abroad and using social media for two years. The court has ordered the seizure of his assets.
Panahi’s lawyer, Mostafa Nili, told Emtedad News Agency that the latest verdict was issued in the filmmaker’s absence. Nili said Panahi’s bank accounts were unexpectedly frozen last week, prompting the legal team to contact Tehran’s prosecutor’s office, where they learned of the ruling.
The enforcement of both prison sentences remains at the discretion of the Iranian authorities.
Panahi has a long history of clashes with Iranian authorities. In 2010, he was banned from making films, speaking to the media and travelling abroad. Despite the restrictions, he continued making films in secret.
Known for films including The Circle , Offside , This Is Not a Film , Taxi and No Bears , Panahi was arrested in 2022 in connection with protests involving a group of filmmakers. He was released about seven months later.
Restrictions preventing him from making films and travelling abroad were lifted in April 2023, allowing him to attend the Cannes Film Festival and present his film It Was Just an Accident . He later travelled to several countries to promote the drama, which follows a group of former prisoners as they confront their feelings towards a guard who tortured them.
Despite his existing one-year prison sentence and rising tensions in Iran, Panahi chose to return home after completing his international promotional tour, according to Variety .

item.title: ‘Mirzapur’ tops IMDb’s Indian streaming series rankings
item.description:
Mirzapur has appeared on IMDb’s annual list of India’s most popular web series nine times over the past decade, according to a report released by the platform.
Titled 10 Years of Streaming in India — An IMDb Report 2026 , the report examines popular Indian web series from 2016 to 2026. Published on Tuesday, it covers 110 chart positions across 64 titles, with rankings based on page views on IMDb, the Amazon-owned entertainment database.
Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story also performed consistently, appearing on the annual charts five times despite having only one season.
The year-by-year rankings reflect changing audience preferences. TVF’s Pitchers topped the chart in 2016, followed by Prime Video’s Inside Edge in 2017. Netflix’s Sacred Games led in both 2018 and 2019.
Scam 1992 topped the rankings in 2020, followed by TVF’s Aspirants in 2021 and Criminal Justice in 2022. Prime Video’s Farzi led in 2023, while Mirzapur took the top spot in 2024.
The Ba*ds of Bollywood topped the 2025 chart, while Pritam and Pedro was the most popular Indian series from 2026 through October 15.
TVF emerged as a major contributor to the streaming industry, with nine distinct series accounting for 17 chart entries. Its presence on the rankings spanned a decade, from Pitchers in 2016 to Sapne vs Everyone in 2026.
The report also highlighted actors Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, Vikrant Massey, Jitendra Kumar, Kapil Sharma, and Sunil Grover for their repeated appearances in popular streaming productions.
Kay Kay Menon, Naveen Kasturia and Mona Singh were recognised for their versatility, while Shahid Kapoor, Vijay Sethupathi, Samantha, Barun Sobti and Karan Tacker were noted for taking on varied roles across different formats.
Despite growing audience engagement, the number of new streaming series and seasons commissioned in India has declined for two consecutive years. Commissions fell from 202 in 2023 to 169 in 2024 and 145 in 2025. Hindi-language productions accounted for 66% of Indian streaming originals in 2025.
Overall, the report estimates that audience engagement with Indian web series has increased approximately 17-fold over the past decade.
Yaminie Patodia, head of IMDb India, said the report builds on the platform’s previous research into Indian cinema, using IMDb data to examine how streaming has transformed audience interests.
The report also includes insights from industry figures, including Gaurav Gandhi of Prime Video, Gunjan Soni of YouTube, Monika Shergill of Netflix, former Applause Entertainment chief executive Sameer Nair and Vijay Koshy of TVF.

item.title: Where can battery-run rickshaws operate under new rules?
item.description:
Battery-run rickshaws will be barred from national highways, expressways, elevated expressways and Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) roads under new regulations issued by the government to regulate their movement and restore order on city streets.
The Local Government Division under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives issued the regulations through a notification on Thursday.
Titled City Corporation Areas Three-Wheeled Low-Speed Battery-Run Rickshaw Movement Regulations, 2026, the rules will apply to battery-run rickshaws operating in all city corporation areas across the country.
Under the regulations, the relevant authorities and traffic departments will jointly designate routes by zone. Rickshaws operating in one zone will not be allowed to enter another, and drivers must keep to the left lane.
The rules also prohibit horns exceeding 40 decibels. In areas near schools, hospitals, places of worship and other crowded locations, the maximum permitted speed will be 15km per hour.
Driving on footpaths, using mobile phones while driving, and unauthorised overtaking or lane changes will be prohibited.
Rickshaws will also be restricted in the number of passengers and the goods they can carry. They may carry either two or four passengers, in addition to the driver, while commercial goods other than passengers’ hand-carried belongings will not be allowed.
The regulations also set out requirements for battery charging and disposal. Batteries may only be charged at authorised charging points or garages. Authorities will gradually move to make net metering, solar panels and renewable energy mandatory at charging stations.
Discarded or non-functional batteries must not be dumped in open spaces, on the ground or in water bodies, or burned. Battery sellers will be required to take back an old battery whenever they sell a new one.

item.title: A final call for help, then a death under suspicion
item.description:
A desperate video call to her father, a plea to be rescued from alleged abuse and an abrupt disconnection were among the last known moments of 24-year-old Jumratun Nessa Barsha, whose death at her husband’s home in Dhaka has prompted a murder investigation.
Barsha had called her family around midnight on Tuesday, crying and asking to be taken home, according to her relatives. She reportedly feared she would be killed if she remained there.
When her parents rushed to the house in Monipuripara, they found an ambulance waiting outside. Her in-laws told them she had died by suicide.
At Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, the family learned that Barsha was dead.
Police have since arrested her husband, Nabid Hossain, following a complaint filed by her father, Sheikh Monowar Hossain.
Tejgaon police station Officer-in-Charge Muniruzzaman told Dhaka Tribune on Thursday that Barsha had allegedly been subjected to repeated assaults over dowry demands.
Injury marks were found on her body, he said.
Nabid was arrested at the hospital and produced before a court. The investigation is continuing.
The family disputes the account of suicide given by Barsha’s in-laws and alleges that she was killed following prolonged abuse.
Police have not yet established the cause of death.
Barsha and Nabid married about a year ago after a relationship.
According to her father, trouble began after the marriage when Nabid repeatedly demanded money from his wife’s family.
He alleged that Nabid, who was unemployed, sought financial assistance on several occasions. The family initially gave him money, but the demands continued, frequently leading to arguments and physical abuse.
Relatives said Nabid had also sought money to start a business and buy a motorcycle.
On Tuesday night, Barsha was allegedly assaulted again.
Her family said someone from her in-laws’ household recorded part of the incident and sent the footage to them. The contents and authenticity of the recording have not been independently established.
Around midnight, Barsha contacted her parents through a video call.
She was crying, describing the alleged abuse and asking them to take her away, her family said.
The call suddenly ended.
Alarmed, her parents left for Monipuripara, reaching the house at approximately 12:30am.
An ambulance was parked outside.
According to the family, Barsha’s in-laws claimed she had taken her own life and was being taken to hospital.
Her parents followed the ambulance to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where they learned of her death.
The discovery of injuries on Barsha’s body has added to questions surrounding the circumstances of her death.
Her father’s complaint alleges that she was killed following repeated dowry-related abuse.
Police have arrested Nabid, but the allegations against him have not been proved in court.
Investigators must now establish what happened after Barsha’s final video call, examine the reported footage and determine whether the physical evidence supports the family’s allegations or the account given by her in-laws.
No statement from Nabid or his family responding to the allegations was available in the reports reviewed.
For Barsha’s parents, the unanswered questions begin with the call they received that night, when their daughter asked them to bring her home, but they could not reach her in time.

item.title: The controversy behind the attention on Tahsif Souri’s death
item.description:
The discovery of former Bangladesh Air Force flight lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri’s body in Dhaka’s Turag River has drawn widespread attention, not only because of the unexplained circumstances surrounding his death but also because of his name’s earlier association with a controversial video of Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh during the August 2024 mass uprising.
Tahsif, 28, was found dead on Wednesday, a day after leaving his Uttara home to meet a younger acquaintance. His father has alleged murder, while police have yet to establish the cause of death.
The former officer had previously been named in media reports alleging that he was involved in recording or circulating footage of the then-prime minister’s departure from the country on August 5, 2024.
He had questioned those allegations, while the Inter-Services Public Relations Directorate (ISPR) rejected separate claims that his departure from the Air Force was linked to a foreign intelligence agency.
The controversy has resurfaced following his death, prompting renewed public discussion about his military career and the circumstances in which he left the service.
However, investigators have not established any connection between those earlier events and his death.
Tahsif first drew public attention following allegations that he was involved in recording or circulating footage of Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh as her government collapsed amid the mass uprising on August 5, 2024.
The video circulated widely on social media, prompting questions about who had recorded and released it.
A subsequent media report identified Tahsif and another Air Force officer, Flight Lieutenant Rifat Ashrafi, in connection with the controversy.
The report also alleged that the two officers had been forced into retirement because of suspected links with a foreign intelligence agency.
However, ISPR rejected that allegation in a statement issued on August 4, 2025.
It said the two officers had been retired through due process under the Air Force’s existing laws and regulations in a different context.
Tahsif himself questioned the claims about the video.
In an interview published on a YouTube channel earlier this year, he challenged those making the allegation to provide evidence that he had recorded or circulated the footage.
He also suggested that the controversy might have contributed to his departure from the Air Force, although he did not establish that as a fact.
Tahsif’s father said the family had been informed that his son was removed from the Air Force over disciplinary issues in September 2024.
Following his departure, Tahsif worked with several organisations, including the Bangladesh Cricket Board and Netra News, according to his family.
Relatives and former colleagues said the loss of his position had affected him deeply.
A former colleague told BBC Bangla that Tahsif had accumulated around 200 hours of flying experience and considered becoming a pilot his dream career.
The colleague also said Tahsif faced social pressure following allegations published about him.
His father said Tahsif occasionally expressed apprehension but had not disclosed any specific threat.
These accounts provide background to the public interest surrounding his death, but they do not establish how or why he died.
The case now centres on several unanswered questions: whom Tahsif met after leaving home, where he went that night, what happened after his final message and how his body ended up in the Turag.
His father’s allegation of murder remains unproven, while the initial inquest does not establish a definitive cause of death.
The controversy surrounding his Air Force career has made the case unusually prominent, but any suggestion that it motivated his death would be premature without supporting evidence.
For now, the public attention surrounding Tahsif Souri’s death reflects both the unanswered circumstances of his final hours and the unresolved questions about a controversial chapter of his past.

item.title: NCP to demonstrate at Shahbagh on Friday, calling on at least 3 ministers to resign
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has called a mass protest at Shahbagh on Friday, pressing a five-point charter of demands led by the resignation of Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and Energy Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood.
In a message issued Thursday night, the party said it was demanding the two ministers step down for failing to ensure public safety and energy security.
Among the other demands, the NCP called for dissolving the "one-party-dominated" committee on constitutional amendment and forming a constitutional reform council in line with the referendum verdict.
The party also demanded the repeal of all laws that run counter to human rights and freedom of expression, and insisted that the proposed amendments to the Cyber Security Act must not be passed.
It further called for completing the trials over the July mass killings and implementing the verdicts without delay, and for the removal of the Inspector General of Police (IGP) over what it termed questionable remarks on extrajudicial killings.
Speaking to UNB, NCP Joint Convener Sarwar Tusher said party leaders and other members of its political council would gather at Shahbagh for the protest over the five demands.
"This should not be called a grand rally," he said, adding that the program would begin in Dhaka and be followed by similar protests in divisional cities in phases.
He said the party plans to hold a large-scale rally after the protest programs conclude.

item.title: Therapy centre offers new hope to people with disabilities in Gaibandha
item.description:
A specialised therapy centre in Gaibandha is helping people with disabilities regain mobility and improve their quality of life, bringing rehabilitation services closer to underserved communities in the northern district.
The Friendship Therapy Centre, established in 2023, provides rehabilitation support to children and adults with physical and neurological disabilities, including those who have difficulty moving their limbs or carrying out everyday activities.
The initiative, run by development organisation Friendship, has enabled several patients to regain movement and perform daily activities with greater independence, according to rehabilitation officials and beneficiaries.
Among them is 45-year-old Raja Mia, a resident of Char Ratanpur, whose life changed following an accident four years ago.
“After the accident, I could not move properly. But after receiving services from the therapy centre, I can now walk and move around. I am doing reasonably well,” he said.
His wife described the difficulties the family faced before he began receiving rehabilitation services.
“He used to remain bedridden and could not move his arms or legs. We have been receiving treatment from the Friendship Therapy Centre for the past two years. Now he can move around,” she said.
However, she said her husband still requires advanced medical treatment to make further progress in his recovery.
Farhana Ashrekin, rehabilitation officer at the Friendship Therapy Centre in Gaibandha, said the organisation launched its rehabilitation program in 2020, while the dedicated therapy centre began operations in 2023.
“Since then, we have been providing therapy services to children and adults with neurological impairments and difficulties moving their arms and legs,” she said.
She said regular therapy had helped many patients improve muscle movement and functional mobility.
“Some patients who previously remained bedridden are now able to sit up, while others have gradually regained the ability to stand and walk,” she added.
The program is particularly significant for people living in remote char areas, where access to specialised healthcare and rehabilitation services remains limited.
Matiar Rahman, chairman of Kamarjani Union Parishad under Gaibandha Sadar upazila, said Friendship’s activities had improved access to services and assistance for people with disabilities in the area.
He said the organisation had distributed wheelchairs and recreational materials while working closely with the union parishad to identify people requiring support.
“Friendship’s work for people with disabilities in our union is commendable. We are working together to ensure they receive the assistance they need,” he said.
According to the chairman, approximately 350 people with disabilities live in Kamarjani union.
He said coordination with Friendship had made it easier for local authorities to identify eligible beneficiaries and facilitate access to government disability allowances.
The organisation has also supported an educational initiative called Baranda School in Koraibari, providing learning opportunities for children with disabilities.
Rahman called for the establishment of a dedicated school for children with disabilities in the union.
“My dream is to establish a model school for children with disabilities in Kamarjani,” he said.
He also urged the authorities to introduce larger, specially equipped boats to ensure safer transportation and evacuation for people with disabilities during floods, a recurring challenge in the riverine region.
Barrister Ayesha Taasin Khan, senior director and head of Inclusive Citizenship at Friendship, said the therapy centre had helped change attitudes towards disability within families.
She said parents and other family members were becoming more optimistic as they witnessed improvements in the physical abilities and daily functioning of children receiving rehabilitation support.
“The way we are caring for and giving importance to children with disabilities is creating greater hope among their family members,” she said.
Khan said the initiative had originally been designed to serve residents of remote char communities, but demand had expanded beyond those areas.
“We initially planned to provide services only to char residents. However, people from the mainland are also coming to the therapy centre for treatment,” she said.
Describing the growing demand as a significant development, she expressed hope that similar centres could be established in other underserved areas with government support.
She said expanding rehabilitation facilities would help more people with disabilities access essential services closer to their homes.

item.title: NBR: 10-30 count cotton yarn refers to single count yarn
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has issued a clarification regarding the order concerning the withdrawal of bond facilities and the provision for importing 10–30 count cotton yarn against bank guarantees.
According to an order issued on Thursday (29 October), the "10–30 count cotton yarn" mentioned in two previous directives specifically refers to 10–30 single count cotton yarn.
Signed by NBR Second Secretary (Customs: Export and Bond) Kazi Raihanuzzaman, the order noted that on 7 September, the bond facility for importing 10–30 count cotton yarn was withdrawn to protect local industry interests and streamline raw material access for genuine exporters.
Under that rule, genuine exporters holding warehouse licenses were permitted to import against bank guarantees. The order was subsequently amended on 8 October.
The directive further stated that these measures were adopted in line with decisions made at the first meeting of an inter-ministerial committee formed to review and resolve existing issues in the textile sector.
Issued under the powers conferred by Section 266 of the Customs Act, 2023, the order takes effect immediately.

item.title: Bata Bangladesh reports 189% EPS growth in Q3 2026
item.description:
Bata Bangladesh, a leading footwear brand, reported year-on-year turnover growth of 15% in the third quarter of 2026 (July–September), with YTD growth 11%, reflecting the resilience of its core business amid challenging global and domestic economic conditions.
The company recorded quarterly turnover of Tk211 crore with Tk779.8 crore in YTD.
Persistent inflation continued to constrain household spending, while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and other global uncertainties pushed up energy, production, logistics, and raw material costs.
From January to September 2026, company had a total profit of TK45.4 crore after tax, with earnings per share (EPS) rose to Tk33.2, which is 256% growth from the same period last year.
The company remains focused on sustaining its business momentum through new product introductions, expansion into new retail locations, retail transformation and stronger omnichannel integration.
Bata is also strengthening its digital and e-commerce platforms to make shopping more convenient and accessible for customers nationwide.
Ongoing initiatives to improve cost efficiency and optimize sourcing are expected to support further gains in profitability by the end of 2026.
Commenting on the results, Faria Yasmin, managing director of Bata Bangladesh, said: “Despite global geopolitical tensions and persistent inflationary pressures, Bata Bangladesh has maintained its business momentum and delivered encouraging turnover growth till Q3. Our continued focus on expanding our retail presence, introducing new products that combine comfort and style, and engaging younger and fashion-conscious consumers remains central to our growth strategy. We are also committed to enhancing the customer experience through our digital platforms and omnichannel initiatives.”
Demonstrating its commitment to shareholder returns, Bata Bangladesh also declared an interim cash dividend of 36.3%.
With a continued focus on customer-centric innovation, retail expansion, digital transformation and operational efficiency, Bata Bangladesh aims to strengthen its market position and build sustainable growth for the remainder of 2026.

item.title: TikTok releases Q2 2026 community guidelines enforcement report
item.description:
TikTok on Thursday released its Q2 2026 Community Guidelines Enforcement Report, highlighting the platform’s ongoing commitment to creating a safe digital space for its users.
The report covers data from April to June 2026 and details the proactive steps TikTok has taken to identify and remove content that violates its Community Guidelines.
These measures aim to ensure a positive experience for its global community.
In Q2 2026, TikTok removed a total of 14,791,485 videos in Bangladesh for violating its Community Guidelines.
This represented approximately 0.9% of all content uploaded to the platform.
TikTok proactively identified and removed 99.8% of these videos before users reported them.
Of the proactively removed videos, 92.7% were taken down within 24 hours of posting, and a total of 205,001 videos were later restored to the platform.
Globally, TikTok removed 188 million (188,298,141) videos, equivalent to approximately 0.5% of all content uploaded to the platform.
Of these, 183,344,707 videos were removed through automated detection technologies.
The global proactive removal rate stood at 99.5%, with 92.7% of videos removed within 24 hours. A total of 6,262,383 videos were reinstated after review.
During Q2 2026, TikTok’s AI systems became increasingly effective at identifying and removing older content.
TikTok also removed comments that violated its policies on potentially offensive or inappropriate content.
Globally, a total of 278,384,463 comments were removed in Q2 2026, up from 237,517,128 in Q1 2026.
The platform also removed 146,807,400 fake accounts during the quarter.
An additional 26,840,767 accounts suspected of belonging to users under the age of 13 were removed to help protect younger users.
The report provides further details on the types of content removed for violating TikTok’s policies. Sensitive or mature themes accounted for 19.5% of removed videos.
Another 13.7% violated the platform’s safety and civility standards. Of the removed videos, 13.5% were identified as containing dangerous activities and challenges, and 13.8% involved body exposure and sexualized behaviors.
Meanwhile, 1.8% of the videos removed were flagged as edited media and AI-generated content (AIGC).
The periodic publication of the Community Guidelines Enforcement Report offers insights into the scale and nature of content and account actions, underscoring TikTok's commitment to full transparency.
For detailed insights into the Q2 202 6 report and to learn more about TikTok's content guidelines, tools, and policies, visit TikTok's Transparency Centre, available in Bangla and English .

item.title: Three fires in nine days leave 12 burned in Gazipur
item.description:
Twelve people, including children, have suffered burns in three separate fire incidents in Gazipur over the past nine days, raising concerns over gas leaks and fire safety in residential areas.
All the injured are receiving treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka, the institute’s resident surgeon Dr Sultan Mahmud Sikder confirmed.
In the first incident, three members of the same family suffered severe burns in a gas leak explosion in the Cherag Ali Market area of Tongi around 6:00am on October 21.
According to hospital sources, 85% to 95% of their bodies were burned. All three remain in critical condition, with two receiving treatment in the emergency department and the third in the High Dependency Unit (HDU).
On October 23, four members of another family suffered burns in a fire at their home in Gazipur.
Preliminary information suggests the fire started on a sofa early that morning before spreading to the wooden ceiling, two motorcycles parked on the balcony and eventually the entire house. The exact cause of the fire remains unknown. The injured were initially taken to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital before being transferred to the burn institute for advanced treatment.
Of the four, the mother and elder son have been admitted, while the father and younger son are under observation. The injured include two children aged four and five. One sustained burns to 40% of his body, while the other two family members suffered burns to 2% and 12% of their bodies, respectively.
In the latest incident, five members of the same family were burned in a fire caused by a gas leak in the Sardagong area of Kashimpur, Gazipur, around 8:30am on Thursday. They were brought to the burn institute in Dhaka around 2:00pm.
The family’s head, 40-year-old Riazul Sheikh, suffered burns to around 40% of his body and is in critical condition.
Arifa Begum suffered burns to 5% of her body, while 17-year-old Faria sustained burns to 8%. Eighteen-year-old Rozina and one-year-old Mohammad Rahim each suffered burns to less than 1% of their bodies.
All five are receiving treatment and remain under medical observation.
